articles.title: Cole Palmer: Chelsea attacker ready to put troublesome 2025/26 season behind him after promising start under Xabi Alonso
articles.summary: Cole Palmer impressed during Xabi Alonso's first Premier League win as Chelsea boss against Fulham; Palmer revealed the 'freedom' he feels playing under the Spaniard; watch Chelsea vs Brighton live on Super Sunday from 1pm on Sunday, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
The 24-year-old endured a difficult 2025-26 season, picking up a groin issue which saw him play just twice between August and December.

And while he ended up with 10 Premier League goals, a run of one goal in eight games to end the campaign saw him miss out on England's World Cup squad.

Palmer put that disappointment behind him on Monday as he got off the mark in the Blues' opener against Fulham en route to a 3-2 win. His performance was a reminder of his star quality.

"Physically I feel good, probably the best I've felt in ages, but I think I can [get fitter] with games and more minutes," Palmer told Sky Sports .

"Before my groin injury, I'd never really been injured. Well, rarely [injured]. So then I would just come back and play when I shouldn't have played.

"Obviously the World Cup was coming up, so I was in a bit of a dilemma thinking: 'if I don't play I'm not going to go. But if I play then, I can't play [properly]'.

"It was just a bit of a sticky situation. I didn't really know how to deal with it, but it's one of those things. I was just seeing different people, getting different ideas of why I was injured and what it was.

"Since I've come back I've been working every day to obviously stop it happening again. I just want to stay injury free, and if I'm on the pitch then I know what I can do."

Alonso giving Palmer the keys to freedom

While it is early days, Palmer appears to have been given the license to express himself once again under Alonso.

At times during the tenures of Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior, suggestions were made that Palmer was being shackled as a result of more rigid systems. He even alluded to that himself, but revealed it was no longer the case following conversations with his new boss.

"He [Alonso] just said I'd have more freedom to drift about the pitch. Just like you saw [against Fulham] with the goal I scored.

"Last season, I wouldn't have even made that run because it's not a 'safe zone'. But he's saying move across that zone, drop into play, come get on the ball, create and just do what you do."

That new sense of freedom could help forge lethal attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and new signing Morgan Rogers . All three scored at Craven Cottage and have since been dubbed 'JP Morgan.'

While Palmer is absolutely not a fan of the name, he is excited by the budding relationship between the trio.

"It's a rubbish name. We need to come up with something better than that," he joked. "I think we've got a different mix of qualities. Joao can do a bit of everything. Morgan's more physical and I'm more technical, so I think we've got a good balance."

The win over Fulham gave Chelsea the perfect start, and with Alonso's expertise and no European football, some have tipped the Blues to become surprise title contenders.

Speaking on Monday Night Football , Gary Neville did suggest that the strength of Arsenal could be too much to overcome. However, he felt that Chelsea were in a good place and backed them to make a push for second place.

Regardless, Palmer revealed that no discussion had taken place within the dressing room regarding the table.

"We've not even spoken about it," Palmer said. "You can't say title race yet, we've only played one game."

However, when asked if he believed the quality was in the squad to challenge, Palmer responded: "Yeah, I think so."

articles.body:
Poliana Rocha e a make para show de Leonardo na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Poliana Rocha publicou nas redes sociais o look escolhido para acompanhar o show do marido, Leonardo, na Festa do Peão de Barretos . O cantor é a primeira atração do Palco Estádio neste sábado (29). O destaque do look, predominantemente marrom, é uma bolsa de grife avaliada em torno de R$ 35 mil.

Nos acessórios, ela escolheu um chapéu marrom no mesmo tom da calça. O grande destaque do look foi uma bolsa grifada de couro avaliada em torno de R$ 35 mil e joias prateadas, como colar, pulseira e anel. Na maquiagem, optou por uma produção mais leve e clean.

Poliana Rocha elegante em look marrom e bege para ver Leonardo na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

O último sábado da 71ª edição da Festa do Peão de Barretos tem casa cheia. Todos os ingressos foram vendidos antecipadamente.

A programação contará com a final da Liga Nacional de Rodeio. No Palco Estádio, apresentam-se Leonardo, João Bosco & Vinícius e a principal atração da noite, o embaixador Gusttavo Lima, que promete um show sem hora para terminar.

articles.title: For at least 1 week, Bill Belichick has quieted the noise at UNC — and even cracked a smile
articles.summary: The Tar Heels played tough defense, didn't kill themselves with huge mistakes or penalties and generally made life tough for TCU. Sounds a lot like a Belichi...
articles.body:
In Ireland. In August. In bad weather. Against an opponent that may turn out to be good but was decidedly awful on Saturday.

Still, forget the caveats and trust your eyes. Was that Bill Belichick cracking a smile after North Carolina's 15-10 win over TCU to begin a season where everyone had already written his coaching obituary?

More importantly, was that a Bill Belichick team? It sure looked like it.

Nasty on defense, well-prepared for everything TCU wanted to do and clutch in the red zone, particularly in fourth quarter when the Tar Heels needed stops to win the game.

What does it mean? Maybe nothing. Maybe everything.

But it was unquestionably a program that looked like it has come a million miles from last season when Belichick put together a bumbling mess of a football team — an expensive one, too — that made his college football experiment look like a lost cause.

From all outward appearances, the offseason hadn't gone much better. Mike Lombardi, Belichick's buddy/general manager, was put on paid leave after a human resources complaint by a former staffer. Stephen Belichick, the coach's son and defensive coordinator, went on medical leave for reasons that haven't been made public and hasn't been with the team for weeks. Just like last year, Belichick brought in a whole bunch of new players but his roster was so poorly regarded that the media picked North Carolina 15th out of 17 in the ACC preseason poll.

And then he got on a plane across the Atlantic and shut the critics up, at least for a little while. It's what the greats tend to do. Did you think the guy won six Super Bowls by accident?

Look, there are plenty of reasons to suspect that what happened Saturday was a bit of an Irish mirage. Week 1 games (or Week Zero, in this case) are often misleading. This particular game, given the travel and other factors that come along with such a unique trip, has proven in the past to not be very good at foreshadowing the rest of the season. And just to drive him the point again, TCU was bad Saturday — so bad in terms of penalties and execution issues and uninspired play-calling that you might start to hear some Sonny Dykes hot-seat talk if this was an indicator of what they're going to be.

But if you're a North Carolina fan or administrator, you have to hope that this is finally proof of concept for what Belichick can do in college football now that he's had a year to figure out what kind of players and organization he needs to win.

The Tar Heels still have a tough schedule ahead and plenty of work to do. Bobby Petrino's offense only generated 90 rushing yards behind a pretty new offensive line, and they only converted 3-of-11 third downs.

The bottom line, though, is that North Carolina only committed three penalties, was solid on special teams and didn't kill itself with huge mistakes. It looked like a well-coached team, which was always the theory of Belichick taking over a college football program for the first time in his mid-70s.

For all the talk about being the NFL's 33rd team — which was Lombardi's phrase and his folly — they didn't need to beat the Tennessee Titans to make the Belichick hire worthwhile. They just needed to be relentlessly competent enough to beat most of the teams in the ACC.

Of course, everyone lost focus of that last season amidst the industry-wide schadenfreude of the most successful coach in NFL history falling on his face in college football. Between Lombardi being insufferable, the Tar Heels overpaying for a bad roster and the various oddities around Belichick's girlfriend, Jordon Hudson, it was easier to crack jokes than acknowledge that the team actually improved a bit in the second half of the season and became more competitive than it had any right to be.

Though the hype had evaporated — and rightly so — Belichick actually had some interesting things to say at ACC media days last month if you were willing to listen.

"It wasn't like I learned a new sport, like I'm coaching soccer or something," Belichick said. "The thing I learned the most about was just the people in the university that you build relationships with — the training staff, the academics, the people you work with in other departments, athletic directors. So it's working with everybody and trying to get things done as efficiently and quickly and productively as possible. They've all been great to work with, but there's also a learning curve."

For people inured to the way college sports work, it would be easy to hear that and roll their eyes. They grew up with the complexities of melding an organization that looks like professional football with the nuts and bolts of university life; Belichick did not.

And despite all the changes in how players are recruited and compensated to make college football look more like the NFL, that part of it is very real. Do you think Bill Belichick ever had a conversation with an academic advisor before last year?

It takes a village to make a college football program work. It's an adjustment. And rather than mocking him for it, it actually took a lot of self-awareness for Belichick to recognize how much he had to learn.

Still, before Saturday, there wasn't much evidence that this unusual marriage might work out. It would have been difficult to find anyone in college football that would have predicted an upset over TCU. But it was easy to find people offering anonymous quotes about how this would be Belichick's last year.

Maybe it will be when it's all said and done. There's a long season ahead. North Carolina could still crash and burn and prove the doubters right.

But after the first game of the college football season, it's probably worth dialing back the hot takes about a Belichick implosion.

On Saturday, he didn't look like a 74-year-old on the verge of imploding into retirement. On the contrary: He looked like someone who might have finally got his program going.

articles.standfirst: Los blanquiazules regresan al Bernabéu ocho años después
articles.summary: Los blanquiazules regresan al Bernabéu ocho años después
articles.body: El Real Madrid afronta su segundo partido en casa de la temporada tras haber ganado sus dos primeros encuentros. El Málaga, por su parte, viene de empatar contra el Deportivo de A Coruña y buscará sacar algo positivo del Santiago Bernabéu en su regreso ocho años después. Cómo llega el Real Madrid al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Málaga Los de Mourinho llevan pleno en las dos primeras jornadas disputadas. Se llevó los tres puntos en el RCDE Stadium gracias a un gol en los minutos finales de Carlos Espí, y los otros tres los obtuvo de manera más holgada al golear 4-1 a la Real Sociedad con un hat trick de Mbappé. Las siete bajas que tiene la primera plantilla dejan a Mourinho sin apenas margen de maniobra. A la espera de recuperar a Endrick (el que más cerca está de volver), Mendy, Asencio, Militao, Thiago Pitarch, Rodrygo y Tchouaméni, el entrenador luso se vuelve a apoyar en los mismos tres canteranos: Mario Rivas, Cestero y Alexis Ciria y con la novedad de Javi Navarro en portería. Cómo llega el Málaga al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Real Madrid El conjunto blanquiazul aún no sabe lo que es ganar este curso en LaLiga. Perdió por 2-0 en el debut en el Metropolitano frente al Atlético de Madrid y luego se tuvo que conformar con un punto contra el Deportivo en casa (1-1). El partido entre Real Madrid y Málaga de la jornada 3 de LaLiga EA Sports se juega hoy domingo 30 de agosto a las 17:00 horas. El partido entre Real Madrid y Málaga de la jornada 3 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través del canal Movistar LaLiga. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles.

articles.title: Un error demasiado Caro... antes de que Yáser Asprilla destroce a Las Palmas
articles.standfirst: El Girona aprovechó un error del portero para construir su goleada a una UD que acabó con diez por la expulsión de Jesé con roja directa
articles.summary: El Girona aprovechó un error del portero para construir su goleada a una UD que acabó con diez por la expulsión de Jesé con roja directa
articles.body: El Girona goleó a Las Palmas demostrando que cuando quiere, puede ser letal. Los catalanes hicieron un buen primer tiempo, pero sólo se fueron al vestuario con 1-0 gracias a un golazo de Jastin. Iván Jaime lo empató en la primera acción del segundo acto después de un error de Gazzaniga, pero Caro, que devolvió el error, y Asprilla, con un doblete y un auténtico vendaval, permitieron a los blanquirrojos sumar los tres puntos. Fran Beltrán hizo el 2-1 y el cafetero puso tierra de por medio hasta el 4-1. Al final, Miyashiro recortó distancias e Izan puso el 5-2 definitivo. La primera parte fue dominada, en casi todos los aspectos, por un Girona que impuso el ritmo del juego y, poco a poco, pisó con más asiduidad el área rival. La defensa adelantada de Las Palmas cada vez tenía más trabajo ante un ataque formado por Vanat y Abel Ruiz, muy móvil y que rompía al espacio junto con los extremos Bryan Gil y Jastin. Maduró el partido el cuadro blanquirrojo hasta que Jastin recibió escorado a la izquierda y en el objetivo de buscar el espacio en diagonal dejó atrás a un par de rivales para armar la pierna y soltar un disparo que después de tocar en el palo izquierdo de Caro se coló en la portería canaria. El gol le sentó de maravilla a los de Quique Álvarez, que tres minutos después pudieron hacer el segundo cuando Izan controló con el pecho y sin bote previo hizo lucir para la foto a Caro, esta vez eficaz en su estirada. Lejos de reaccionar, Las Palmas no pudo ni supo inquietar la defensa local, que también estuvo cerca del segundo a través de Bryan Gil y Vanat. Justo en el inicio del segundo tiempo, Las Palmas empató aprovechando el enésimo regalo de Gazzaniga a un rival. Iván Jaime, bien posicionado, superó al argentino, que rechazó un centro como no se debe hacer nunca, dejando el balón muerto en la frontal de la pequeña. Por suerte catalana, Caro devolvió el favor con un mal pase que Fran Beltrán coló a la red picando por encima del guardameta. Y con el viento de nuevo a favor, el huracán Asprilla cerró el partido con un doblete. El primero, sacando las telarañas de la escuadra después de una transición, y el segundo aprovechando una asistencia de Abel Ruiz. Miyashiro batió a Gazzaniga desde la frontal e Izan, ya al final, y con un Las Palmas entregado jugando con diez por la expulsión de Jesé, hizo el 5-2 definitivo

articles.title: Furious Liverpool star loses cool and kicks fourth official’s substitution board after controversial penalty in 2-2 draw
articles.summary: Football News: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker expressed his frustration after a controversial penalty decision led to a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest. Alisson kicked the fourth official's substitution board, highlighting his anger over the officiating. The match featured pivotal moments, including a comeback by Liverpool and key contributions from new signing Victor Munoz.
articles.body: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker was left furious after a controversial penalty decision helped Nottingham Forest take the lead at Anfield, and his frustration appeared to boil over after the final whistle as he was reportedly seen kicking the fourth official’s substitution board hard enough to leave a visible hole in it.The incident came during a dramatic 2-2 draw on Saturday, with Liverpool twice forced to fight back after falling behind. The penalty itself became one of the biggest talking points of the match, particularly because of the timing of the decision and the events immediately before it, while Alisson was booked for his furious reaction.How the penalty controversy unfoldedLiverpool and Nottingham Forest were level at 1-1 in the 70th minute when the incident unfolded. Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola had been preparing a triple substitution, but fourth official Tim Robinson was not yet ready with the electronic board.That delay gave Forest the opportunity to restart quickly with a throw-in, with the ball reaching former Liverpool player Neco Williams. Williams moved into the box and was brought down by Alisson, prompting referee Sam Barrott to immediately point to the penalty spot.Liverpool's players and bench erupted in protest, with Alisson particularly angry about the decision. The goalkeeper was shown a yellow card for his reaction, while VAR reviewed the incident but did not overturn Barrott's decision.Alisson did make contact with Williams, although reports noted that the contact appeared minimal, and the decision subsequently drew questions from supporters and observers on social media.Forest made Liverpool pay when Morgan Gibbs-White stepped up and converted the penalty, restoring the hosts' deficit and putting Nottingham Forest 2-1 ahead.Liverpool fight back againLiverpool once again found themselves needing a late response, and just as they had done in their opening league fixture against Newcastle United, the Reds found a way back into the game.Florian Wirtz produced the creative spark in the 82nd minute, threading a through-ball towards substitute Victor Munoz, who took his chance brilliantly and fired into the net to make it 2-2.Munoz has now made an immediate impression in both of his Premier League appearances for Liverpool since arriving from Osasuna for a reported €40 million. Against Newcastle, he came off the bench and won a ninth-minute-of-added-time penalty that Dominik Szoboszlai converted for a 2-2 equaliser, and against Forest he came on again before scoring the goal that rescued another point.Wirtz did have a goal ruled out during the match, with the referee's explanation of that decision later shown to Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk on the ref cam.The result means Iraola's Liverpool have now drawn their first two league matches of the campaign against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, leaving them still searching for their first Premier League victory. Visuals circulating on social media also appeared to show Alisson kicking an fourth official’s substitution board after the final whistle, with the impact leaving a noticeable hole in it.Iraola pleased with Munoz's impactWhile the result left Liverpool frustrated, Munoz's contribution has given Iraola something positive to take from the opening two games.Speaking after the Forest draw, the Liverpool manager praised the winger's persistence and the defensive work he has contributed alongside his attacking threat."I think Victor has been very good (in) both games... Everything hasn't been perfect, but he's continued trying all the time. He's gone again and again and I like this a lot from the wingers. The other day he contributed with the penalty and today with the goal. I think he has been always a threat. And also, defensively he has helped us a lot, so I'm happy with him, yes."Munoz's back-to-back contributions off the bench could now put him in contention for a starting role as Liverpool look for a way to turn their promising late fight-backs into victories.Liverpool still looking to strengthenIraola is also hoping Liverpool can add another winger before the transfer window closes, with the club reportedly pursuing Ismaïla Sarr and Yankuba Minteh after bids for both players were rejected.The Reds are also close to completing the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, with the winger expected to undergo his medical on Sunday and potentially be available for the trip to Ipswich Town on Friday, September 4.Asked about Liverpool's search for another winger earlier this week, Iraola said:"We are trying to sign in that position. We cannot talk about players who are not ours."It is no secret that we are trying to improve to fill those positions because we don't have the numbers. I hope we can have good news but we are not there yet."I don’t know what’s going to happen. We have to patient. I will be comfortable on September 2. Right now, we don’t know. I have in my head what I want, we spoke since the beginning what we want. It’s a matter of closing the deal."Liverpool's immediate concern, however, is turning those draws into wins, with their next Premier League assignment coming away to newly promoted Ipswich Town on September 4.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Independence Football retires Atticus Goodson’s #3 jersey
articles.summary: COAL CITY, WV (WVNS) – Independence High School Football legend Atticus Goodson became the first player in program history to have his jersey retired. This a...
articles.body:
COAL CITY, WV (WVNS) - Independence High School Football legend Atticus Goodson became the first player in program history to have his jersey retired.

This adds to the long line of firsts Goodson brought to the Patriots.

He led Indy to their first state championship game appearance and became the first Raleigh County player to bring home the Kennedy Award since the 1940's. Not to mention, he was the first Patriot player to be selected Captain of the All-State team.

The Patriots held a special ceremony at halftime of their home win against Armstrong to ensure no other player after Micah Cuthbert will wear his jersey number 3.

"One of the only things that I wanted when I started playing football here is I wanted in the Hall of Fame and to have my jersey retired and with all these people here in the stands and everything…it really means a lot," said Goodson.

Goodson helped thrust the program into the winning ways they've become well accustomed to over the last several years.

Looking back, even though Indy never got a title during Atticus's time in red, white, and blue, he shares that he will cherish those memories and the bonds he made with his Independence Football brothers forever.

articles.title: João Bosco & Vinícius gravam DVD de 19 anos em Barretos | G1
articles.standfirst: A dupla gravou "JB&V Ao Vivo em Barretos — A Voz de uma Geração" na madrugada deste domingo (30), na última noite de shows do Estádio. Maria Cecília & Rodolfo subiram ao palco em duas músicas.
articles.summary: João Bosco & Vinícius agitaram a Festa do Peão de Barretos com a gravação do DVD "A Voz de uma Geração", reunindo sucessos e clássicos sertanejos na madrugada.
articles.body:
João Bosco & Vinícius gravaram um novo projeto audiovisual no palco do Estádio da 71ª Festa do Peão de Barretos (SP), na madrugada deste domingo (30). Diante de uma arena lotada, a dupla juntou os próprios sucessos a clássicos de outras gerações do sertanejo e celebrou o que chamou no palco de 19 anos de história com a festa.

O registro se chama "JB&V Ao Vivo em Barretos — A Voz de uma Geração" e foi gravado na última noite de shows do Estádio, entre as apresentações de Leonardo e de Gusttavo Lima, o embaixador desta edição.

O show abriu com "Parece Castigo", seguida de "Ah, É?" e de "Chora, Me Liga", um dos maiores hits da dupla. A arena respondeu em coro logo nos primeiros minutos.

João Bosco & Vinícius no palco da Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

"Estamos felizes com a recepção de vocês, que estão cantando tudo", disse João Bosco.

Na sequência vieram "Segunda Taça", "Falando Sério", "Meu Ex-Amor", "Só Fazendo Amor" e "Preciso Amar de Novo", alternando as músicas dançantes e as baladas românticas que sustentam a carreira da dupla desde o início dos anos 2000.

"Prometemos que este será o nosso melhor show para vocês", disse Vinícius. João Bosco completou: "Essa noite vai ser a melhor noite da vida de vocês".

Logo depois começaram os primeiros acordes de "Página de Amigos", de Chitãozinho & Xororó — a primeira de uma série de homenagens a outras gerações do sertanejo.

Também entraram no repertório "Dou a Vida por um Beijo", de Zezé Di Camargo & Luciano; "Vida Cigana", gravada por João Pedro & Cristiano; "Magia e Mistério", de Guilherme & Santiago; "A Gente Se Entrega", de Rionegro & Solimões; e "Pra Lá de Bagdá", de Gian & Giovani.

A mistura acompanhou toda a apresentação: de um lado, o repertório que construiu a carreira dos dois; de outro, canções que fazem parte da memória do público sertanejo.

João Bosco & Vinícius desfilam hits na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

Os convidados da noite foram Maria Cecília & Rodolfo. A dupla entrou em "Fim da Noite" e ficou para cantar "Você de Volta", a música que projetou os dois para todo o país.

"Que honra receber vocês aqui, hoje, para a gravação deste projeto", disse João Bosco.

Depois, "Deixa a Gente Quieto", "Sufoco", "Tarde Demais", "Abelha" e "Bloqueia Eu" mantiveram a arena cantando. "Quero ver a energia de vocês com João Bosco & Vinícius", pediu João Bosco antes de chamar o público para dançar. Fogos e efeitos de luz acompanharam a sequência.

João Bosco & Vinícius dançam juntos no palco da Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

Em determinado momento, a dupla voltou ao começo da carreira. O primeiro disco, "Acústico no Bar", saiu em 2003, gravado só com voz e violão.

"Quando gravamos nosso primeiro disco, lá no início dos anos 2000, essa moda foi uma das mais tocadas nos carros e botecos de todo o Brasil", disse João Bosco, antes de a dupla cantar "Faz de Conta".

O repertório seguiu com "Tatuagem", "Colo Colo", "Não Era Você", "Sem Esse Coração" e "Como Eu Deixaria Tudo".

João Bosco & Vinícius embalam arena lotana na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

Perto do fim, João Bosco pediu que o público ligasse as lanternas dos celulares. "Essa vai para todas as amigas lindas de Barretos", anunciou, antes de "Amiga Linda", lançada em 2015 no álbum "Estrada de Chão". A arena se iluminou e cantou junto.

A reta final teve "O Fora", "Curtição" e "Ei, Psiu! Beijo Me Liga". Em "Um Lugarzinho na Sua Cama", os dois dançaram juntos no palco, antes de "Eu Vou Morrer de Amor".

"São 19 anos de história com essa festa maravilhosa. Aqui, eternizamos mais uma etapa do nosso sonho. Obrigado, Barretos!", disse João Bosco.

O show terminou como havia começado: com "Chora, Me Liga". O público cantou o refrão mais uma vez antes de a dupla deixar o palco.

articles.title: Liga Nacional de Rodeio: Renan Alves conquista bicampeonato inédito | G1
articles.standfirst: Renan Almeida Alves conquistou 89,75 pontos após ficar oito segundos em cima do touro Águia Negra, da companhia Gutt Bulls na noite deste sábado (29). Ele ganhou R$ 150 mil e uma vaga no The American.
articles.summary: A vitória na Liga Nacional de Rodeio rendeu a Renan Alves R$ 150 mil e uma vaga em competição nos EUA após montaria histórica na Festa do Peão de Barretos.
articles.body:
O peão Renan Almeida Alves, de Orlândia (SP) , tornou-se o primeiro bicampeão da Liga Nacional de Rodeio (LNR) . A final da competição aconteceu na noite deste sábado (29) e reuniu sete atletas. Apenas três conseguiram completar os oito segundos sobre os touros.

Campeão em 2025, Renan chegou à decisão como favorito e em busca de um feito inédito nos 20 anos da LNR. Último a entrar na arena, ele enfrentou o touro Águia Negra, da companhia Gutt Bulls.

Renan Alves conquista bicampeonato inédito da Liga Nacional de Rodeio em Barretos — Foto: Reprodução/BRTVMAX

Em uma montaria de alto nível, o competidor dominou o touro, que girou e saltou intensamente. O desempenho rendeu a Renan a maior nota da noite, 89,75 pontos, e garantiu o título pelo segundo ano consecutivo.

Além da fivela dourada, o campeão recebeu R$ 150 mil e conquistou uma vaga no The American, competição disputada nos Estados Unidos.

Renan Alves conquista bicampeonato inédito da Liga Nacional de Rodeios em Barretos — Foto: Reprodução/BRTVMAX

O segundo lugar ficou com Matheus Henrique Rosa, de Divinópolis (MG). Ele demonstrou domínio sobre o touro Extravagante, da companhia 2M – Marcondes, e recebeu 89,25 pontos.

Matheus Bernardino, de Senador Guiomard (AC), completou o pódio. O peão enfrentou quatro dias de viagem de ônibus para tentar realizar o sonho compartilhado pela família de conquistar a fivela dourada da LNR.

O título não veio, mas a nota de 73,50 pontos obtida sobre o touro Destroyer, da companhia ATF, garantiu ao competidor uma vaga no The American.

Matheus Bernardino, do Acre, terminou em terceiro lugar na final da LNR — Foto: Reprodução/BRTVMAX

O prêmio de melhor touro da edição ficou com Mestre dos Magos, da cia JK Bucking Bulls. Já o de melhor boiada ficou com a companhia HP Bulls.

A final da LNR reuniu peões de todos os cantos do Brasil, classificados ao longo de mais de 120 etapas. Cinco atletas se classificaram após duas classificatórias com 137 competidores. São eles: Adriano Lindoso Silva, Douglas da Silva, Fabiano Silveira, Matheus Bernardino e Matheus Henrique Rosa.

Outros dois competidores se classificaram após uma etapa do Elite ShownDown.

A nova modalidade reuniu competidores que conquistaram mais vitórias ao longo da temporada da LNR. Daniel Henrique Possamai, de Tabapuã/SP, e Matheus Henrique Rosa, de Divinópolis/MG, se classificaram direto para a final após realizarem as melhores montarias da modalidade.

articles.title: Ethan Pritchard Walks Out with FSU in Video Nearly One Year After Being Shot in Head
articles.summary: Florida State linebacker Ethan Pritchard, who survived a gunshot wound to the head on Aug. 31, 2025, walked out with the Seminoles on Saturday prior to their home game against New Mexico State.
articles.body:
Florida State linebacker Ethan Pritchard, who survived a gunshot wound to the head on Aug. 31, 2025 , walked out with the Seminoles on Saturday prior to their home game against New Mexico State.

Pritchard spoke with Spectrum News 13 about the trials and tribulations he went through just to get to this point.

Pritchard was a 3-star linebacker in the class of 2025 out of Seminole High School in Sanford, Florida. He signed with the Seminoles in Dec. 2024.

It's been a tough road for him since the tragedy, but he's been a determined fighter all along the way.

In June, Pritchard spoke with Peter Holland of the Tallahassee Democrat and stated his goal of walking onto Doak Walker Stadium's field for the opener.

"I don't want to put no specific time standpoint, but I will tell you that I'm going to walk out there on the field, come first game. I feel like I already beat the hard part. I beat death. This is just getting my body back."

Pritchard has accomplished the mission and told reporters on Friday how well he was doing.

"I am feeling great, better than ever, better than I did before I got shot," Pritchard said, per Sarah Winkelmann of Spectrum News 13.

Best wishes to Pritchard, of course, as he continues his recovery.

articles.title: Bayern Munich boss scoffs at Michael Olise transfer reports
articles.summary: The FC Bayern exec said losing Michael Olise was never a threat.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen has made it abundantly clear that the club never took the summer reports linking Michael Olise with Real Madrid particularly seriously.

Asked how Bayern Munich followed the constant speculation surrounding their French winger, Dreesen admitted that the reporting could be amusing at times, but also frustrating.

"As someone in charge who also knows the inside story, you sometimes can't help but be amused, and at other times irritated by what gets written. We have always said: It's nonsense. It was nonsense back then, and it still is nonsense," Dreesen said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Olise himself never felt the need to publicly address the rumors, and Dreesen believes that was the right approach. Rather than getting involved in speculation away from the pitch, Olise has allowed his performances to do the talking.

"Firstly, Michael speaks the decisive language on the pitch. Secondly it's good that he's not letting the fuss surrounding him bother him. I'm not even sure he reads all of that or hears about it," Dreesen said.

Dreesen also confirmed that Bayern Munich are not currently negotiating a new contract with Olise. With the 23-year-old already tied down until 2029, there is simply no urgency from the club's perspective.

"No, we are not currently holding any talks. If I remember correctly, Michael still has a contract until 2029. So there's no reason to be hasty or rush anything now,"stated the CEO.

As far as Olise goes, his behavior has been at least a little odd, but he is always at least a little odd . The Frenchman's reactions and actions always keep fans guessing if he is really that aloof or if it is all just an act for the public. Either way, no one will care how bizarre he might come across if he continues to display the kind of excellence he has on the pitch on a regular basis.

articles.title: Erling Haaland's secret weapon is not his goalscoring as Manchester City star reveals the power of his mind
articles.summary: International Sports News: Erling Haaland has never fit neatly into the image of a modern football superstar. Away from the roar of the stadium, the Manchester City striker is o.
articles.body: Erling Haaland has never fit neatly into the image of a modern football superstar. Away from the roar of the stadium, the Manchester City striker is often quiet, reflective and intensely private. Yet his routines reveal a player who leaves little to chance. From meditation and recovery work to his approach to pressure, Haaland has built a mindset that helps explain how he keeps producing at an extraordinary level.Erling Haaland's mentality shapes his approach to footballHaaland's recent YouTube videos have offered fans an unusually close look at the person behind the goals. The Norwegian has shown his training sessions, recovery habits and quieter moments, giving supporters a sense of how much work happens away from match day.His philosophy is strikingly simple.“If you tell yourself you’re tired, you’re going to be tired,” he says in one video while exercising inside a hypoxic chamber. “But if you tell yourself you’re not that tired, you’re not that tired. It’s simple. Our bodies can handle so much more than we think. It’s all psychological. A lot is in the mind.”That belief extends to meditation. Haaland has repeatedly spoken about using it to clear negative thoughts and remain present, particularly when the pressure around him becomes intense.His former coach Alf Ingve Berntsen saw those habits developing from an early age. Haaland was introduced to lessons about nutrition, sleep and football skills while playing at Bryne, long before he became one of the Premier League's most feared forwards.He also had to learn to compete without relying on physical dominance. As a youngster, Haaland was smaller than many players around him and often played against older opponents. Training against older centre-backs helped him understand movement, positioning and how to find space inside the penalty area.Those experiences helped create a player who treats improvement as a daily responsibility rather than something that ends when training does.That attitude remains visible at Manchester City. Haaland has described staying behind to stretch even when he does not feel like doing it.“Do I want to do this?” he asks of the extra work. “No. I don’t. Will I do it? Yeah. It’s good for my body. It’s good for my mind.”Erling Haaland's introversion gives him another edgeHaaland's personality can seem surprising when compared with the traditional image of a star striker. He can be loud and playful with teammates, but he is also comfortable stepping away from the spotlight.Sports psychologist Marc Sagal explained that introversion does not mean an athlete avoids people. Instead, some players simply regain their energy differently. For Haaland, quiet time appears to help him maintain focus in a sport where attention rarely stops.That balance was clear during the 2026 World Cup. Haaland could be highly social with Norway's squad, including taking teammates shopping for cowboy hats, before returning to more private moments of reflection.His self-awareness may be just as important.Haaland once described a season with 21 or 22 goals as a bad one, even while acknowledging that it was still good. The comment showed how high his own standards have become.His approach to mistakes is equally direct. Speaking with Alan Shearer for The Athletic in 2022, Haaland said:“As a striker, I think it’s really important that when you’re in the game, to not think too much,” he says. “If I’m going to go into my next game thinking about the chance I missed last game, it’s not good.“You have to go into the game hungry. It doesn’t matter what happened before. If you scored three goals, if you scored zero goals, if you haven’t scored in a while. You have to go into the game with the same mentality. And so I think about not thinking too much about it! This is also something that helps me a lot; this meditation outside the pitch to just kind of let go of the negative thoughts.”That may be the clearest window into Haaland's mindset. He understands the noise, accepts the expectations and then tries to leave them outside the next match.As one former coach put it, “His strength is not seeing everything in black or white.”For Haaland, success seems to come from holding both sides together: confidence without arrogance, intensity without panic and a superstar profile without losing the ordinary person underneath it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Manchester City make shock move to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool in £85m deal: Reports
articles.summary: Football News: Manchester City has reportedly initiated talks with Liverpool for a stunning £85 million transfer of Dutch forward Cody Gakpo, who's emerged as a prime target before the closing of the transfer window. With Liverpool needing to solidify their attacking lineup, will Gakpo make the switch?
articles.body: Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool over a potential move for Cody Gakpo, with the Dutch forward emerging as one of the biggest names who could still change clubs before the transfer window closes.According to reports, City made formal contact with Liverpool on Saturday evening regarding a move for the 27-year-old. ESPN, citing its own sources, reported that discussions between the clubs had gathered pace and that Liverpool value Gakpo at £85 million ($115m).Gakpo has also attracted interest from Tottenham Hotspur, but sources cited by BBC Sport indicate that Manchester City is the forward's preferred destination should he leave Anfield.Why could Gakpo leave Liverpool?The possibility of Gakpo's departure comes at a particularly interesting point in Liverpool's transfer window. The Reds have agreed a deal to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola for a fee that could rise to £123 million, according to BBC Sport, and Liverpool are understood to want another forward through the door before allowing Gakpo to leave.Liverpool have an interest in Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace forward Ismaïla Sarr, with the club having already seen bids for both players rejected, according to reports.That means Gakpo's situation is not simply a matter of whether City are prepared to meet Liverpool's valuation; the Reds also need to make sure they have sufficient attacking options before sanctioning his exit.ESPN reported that City have been encouraged by Gakpo's interest in a move to the Etihad Stadium and are pressing ahead with negotiations.Gakpo has been an important part of Liverpool's attackGakpo joined Liverpool from his boyhood club PSV Eindhoven in January 2023 and has since scored 33 goals in 91 Premier League appearances.The forward has also started the new season in good form. He scored in Liverpool's opening league fixture, a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United, and then provided the assist for Alexander Isak's goal in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest at Anfield.Gakpo started against Forest despite the growing speculation surrounding his future, with Liverpool twice having to come from behind to rescue a point.His possible departure would therefore leave Andoni Iraola with another significant attacking decision to make, particularly with Liverpool already close to bringing Barcola into the squad.City preparing for a busy finish to the windowManchester City are also expected to remain active during the final days of the transfer window.According to ESPN, City have already agreed a deal with Palmeiras for Brazilian winger Allan, while Savio and Omar Marmoush have both left the club to join Tottenham this summer.The club have also been working on their midfield, having already spent more than £200 million on that area following the departures of Bernardo Silva and Rodri, with Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi among their additions.ESPN's sources say City are expected to make at least one late bid for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernández as well as continuing discussions over Gakpo.For Liverpool, meanwhile, the decision is becoming increasingly time-sensitive, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday, September 1. The club must now weigh City's interest against its own need to maintain numbers in attack, particularly with Barcola's arrival close and further moves for Minteh or Sarr still being pursued.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 0
articles.summary: From sea to shining sea, plus a trip across the pond, the 2026 college football season finally kicked off Saturday with an eight-game schedule.
articles.body:
From sea to shining sea, plus a trip across the pond, the 2026 college football season finally kicked off Saturday with an eight-game schedule.

In the opening game of the FBS campaign—a showdown set in Dublin, Ireland—Bill Belichick and North Carolina started with an overseas victory. The Tar Heels knocked off TCU 15-10.

Saturday's slate also included 14th-ranked USC rolling past San Jose State, and Virginia smoked NC State for a valuable ACC victory. Also of note, Week 0 marked the FBS debuts of North Dakota State and Sacramento State.

And, most importantly, we have college football again.

I will be the first person to raise my hand and say I did not believe—and do not believe—that Bill Belichick is going to work at North Carolina.

Thanks to a 12-10 advantage at the break, UNC led a power-conference opponent at halftime for the first time in Belichick's tenure. The second half brought little scoring, but the Tar Heels left Dublin with a 15-10 victory.

This result does not substantially alter expectations for North Carolina, which had a very limited offense. Don't expect 322 yards to win many games.

For one afternoon, though, UNC had enough. And that didn't happen often in 2025.

If you want the glass-half-full outlook, it wasn't a conference game. TCU's upside as a Big 12 threat, technically speaking, remains intact.

Nevertheless, losing to North Carolina is not exactly the most reassuring thing in the world. TCU's offense mustered just 281 yards and committed two late turnovers on downs in the red zone during this frustrating loss.

On the bright side, the Horned Frogs are entering an idle weekend before hosting Grambling and Arkansas State. They have a window to address the early offensive issues prior to the beginning of Big 12 action. The season is not lost.

Still, that is absolutely not the opener that TCU believed would happen.

As expected, USC cruised to its Week 0 victory.

Jayden Maiava competed 25-of-29 passes for 286 yards and two touchdowns, and the Trojans racked up 505 yards in a 42-26 triumph over San Jose State. It was exactly what USC faithful anticipated in this matchup.

Truly, the margin would've been larger were it not for SJSU's two garbage-time scores. USC held a 31-point lead midway through the fourth quarter.

Winning this contest in that fashion is not a surprise. But as USC eyes a first-ever College Football Playoff trip, a comfortable win against an overmatched opponent is the proper way to kick off the season.

After a breakout 11-win campaign in 2025, the Cavaliers opened the season with a favorable outlook. But with an opening game against North Carolina State, that optimism would be tested immediately.

And Virginia, despite the stakes, left no doubt in a 34-8 rout.

Beau Pribula put together an encouraging debut following his transfer from Missouri, throwing for 155 yards and running for 110 with two scores. The defense straight-up dominated the ACC contest and limited NC State to 168 yards, too.

Miami, SMU, Louisville and Clemson are among the prime ACC contenders this season, but UVA is capable of making another run. Saturday just reinforced that ceiling.

Considering what North Dakota State has accomplished in the FCS lately, no bit of immediate success should be surprising. The program won 10 national championship in the last 16 seasons.

Regardless, this was a tremendously dominant win.

Jacksonville State traveled to the Fargodome and found itself in a terribly unwelcoming environment. NDSU boatraced the visitors 33-7 with 373 offensive yards to a meager 170 for Jax State.

As alluded to several times, it's essential to remember this is Week 0. Any number of grand proclamations have gone horribly wrong in recent years.

But there's no question we should be taking NDSU very seriously.

The essential takeaway of every Week 0 matchup is that we still have a long season ahead. Please do not overreact to these results.

Also, yeah, you can be concerned about Florida State.

As a heavy favorite, the Seminoles meandered to a 34-17 win over New Mexico State. The result was never seriously in jeopardy, yet FSU fell short of an emphatic win. At no point did the 'Noles build a lead greater than 17 points.

The problem, more than anything, is context. Florida State coach Mike Norvell arguably sits on the hottest seat in the country, and anything short of a painless win this weekend would be met with tepid reactions.

Well, it wasn't painless. The vibes around FSU are not amazing right now.

In the last six full seasons, Stanford has finished no better than 4-8. The once-stout program is dealing with a prolonged lull.

That reality was on full display in 2025, and we saw it immediately. Stanford lost its opening game at Hawaii, which used a couple of fourth-quarter field goals to spring a slight 23-20 upset.

Déjà vu seemed it would be making an appearance on Saturday.

Fortunately for the Cardinal, though, they responded when it mattered most. After watching a 23-7 lead crumble into a 27-23 deficit, Stanford managed 14 points in the last two minutes to secure a 37-27 triumph.

The comeback has not abruptly changed Stanford's minor expectations. This is still probably not a bowl team, let alone anything more.

But as first-year coach Tavita Pritchard aims to rebuild the program, every win—no matter the story—is vital to Stanford's future.

articles.title: Michael Carrick says it is ‘lazy’ to claim Man Utd lacked passion after embarrassing 2-0 defeat to newly promoted Hull City
articles.summary: Football News: Michael Carrick has dismissed criticism of Manchester United's lack of passion in their 2-0 defeat to Hull City, stating that the performance goes beyond mere effort. United will face Ipswich Town next as they aim to bounce back from their opening-day setback in the Premier League.
articles.body: Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that Manchester United lacked passion or motivation in their shock opening-day defeat to newly promoted Hull City, calling it “lazy” to reduce the performance to a lack of effort.United began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-0 defeat at the MKM Stadium despite having 71.7% possession, with Hull scoring twice from set pieces in the first half. The result has led to criticism of United's attitude and desire, but Carrick insists there was more to the defeat than simply a failure to try.Carrick rejects claims United lacked desireUnited were accused of lacking passion and intensity during the defeat, but Carrick defended his players ahead of Sunday's home meeting with another newly promoted side, Ipswich Town.“Teams lose games and win games, and it's not just because you try or you don't try,” Carrick told a news conference.“There are all sorts of different reasons. Teams lose games, so there's different reasons. I don't have to give you the total reason, because we know what we're trying to improve on.“I think it's so easy and lazy to just say 'team loses a game, everything's wrong.' This is wrong, this is wrong, not trying enough, not enough passion.”Carrick's comments come after a difficult start in which United dominated possession but struggled to turn that control into enough attacking threat, while two first-half set-piece goals left them chasing the game.Carrick wants United to respondUnited now have the chance to respond immediately when Ipswich visit Old Trafford on Sunday for the club's first home match of the season.Carrick lost only two Premier League games last season, against Leeds United and Newcastle United, and United responded with victories on both occasions. The club went on to finish third in the Premier League in 2025-26, with 20 wins, 11 draws and seven defeats.For Carrick, how his players respond to the Hull setback will say more about them than the defeat itself.“I think success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end,” Carrick added.“In any position, certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there's going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others.“I think it ultimately decides what type of team you're going to become. So far, we've dealt with those setbacks really well, within games, game to game.“We had one last week. No getting away from it and it's disappointing. But we look to bounce back. We had a good week, boys are refocused, learned from where we could have improved, and keep pushing forward.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: North Dakota State defeated Jacksonville State 33-7 on Saturday to mark the beginning of its first-ever season as a Division I-FBS program.
articles.body:
North Dakota State defeated Jacksonville State 33-7 on Saturday to mark the beginning of its first-ever season as a Division I-FBS program.

Here's a look at the stats and some highlights from the game.

Quarterback Nathan Hayes found tight end Reid Kessel for a six-yard touchdown to close NDSU's first drive as an FBS member (the Bison now play in the Mountain West).

Jacksonville State, which plays in Conference USA, countered with its own touchdown.

However, NDSU finished the game with 26 unanswered points. Drew Klein hit four field goals (34, 44, 42 and 48 yards) over the second through fourth quarters.

The touchdowns were courtesy of wide receiver Jordan McCants (on a 44-yard pass from Hayes) and defensive end Blake Schlitz (off a recovered fumble in the end zone after a bad snap).

NDSU won 10 Division I-FCS national championships over a 14-year period (2011-2024). Needless to say, it was probably time for the Bison to move up, and they started their season on a great note.

NDSU will now host Division I-FBS Fordham on Saturday, Sept. 5. Their first Mountain West game will be Saturday, Sept. 12 at Air Force.

articles.title: Lionel Messi Scores 4 Goals, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights as Inter Miami Beats Montreal
articles.summary: Lionel Messi was unstoppable during Inter Miami's 7-1 victory over CF Montréal on Saturday.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi was unstoppable during Inter Miami's 7-1 victory over CF Montréal on Saturday.

Messi finished with four goals in the lopsided win.

Live World Football News and Highlights ⚡

The 39-year-old's first goal came on a deflected free kick in the 40th minute that gave Miami a 2-0 lead.

Messi found the back of the net once again in the 52nd minute, navigating through multiple defenders before finishing with his right foot.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner eventually completed his hat trick with a chip over Montréal goalkeeper Thomas Gillier following a slick feed from Rodrigo De Paul.

Messi capped off the night with a free kick in stoppage time that brought his total to four goals.

Miami's overall performance against Montréal was impressive, holding 57 percent of possession and finishing with 11 shots on goal.

Messi now has 18 goals for Miami this year, leading all MLS players during the 2026 season.

Saturday also marked the eighth occasion in which Messi has scored four or more goals in a single match and his first since he played for Barcelona in 2020 (h/t ESPN ).

The victory also represented Miami's first win since Aug. 5.

articles.title: 4 goals and an assist: How Lionel Messi led Inter Miami to dominant 7-1 MLS win over Montreal
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi delivered a sensational performance as Inter Miami demolished CF Montreal 7-1 on Saturday, scoring four goals and setting up another in a.
articles.body: Lionel Messi delivered a sensational performance as Inter Miami demolished CF Montreal 7-1 on Saturday, scoring four goals and setting up another in a dominant MLS victory. articles.standfirst: MARCA habla con varias de las agencias de futbolistas más importantes a nivel mundial y nacional para saber cómo trabajan, sus relaciones con el jugador, sus responsabilidades en casos como el de Julián Álvarez, y las leyendas en torno a su ecosistema
articles.summary: MARCA habla con varias de las agencias de futbolistas más importantes a nivel mundial y nacional para saber cómo trabajan, sus relaciones con el jugador, sus responsabilidades en casos como el de Julián Álvarez, y las leyendas en torno a su ecosistema
articles.body: En esta vida, hay cosas que todo el mundo da por hecha su existencia, pero que muy poca gente conoce en profundidad. Los océanos, el tiempo como concepto, el cerebro humano, y como no, las agencias de futbolistas. Solemos hablar en la jerga periodística y futbolera de que ‘X’ jugador pertenece a ’X’ agencia, dando por sabido que aquel que se encuentra al otro lado de la pantalla o el papel ubica a cada empresa de representación como si fuese un equipo. Sin embargo, no siempre ocurre así. Y la pregunta que surge entonces es, ¿cuáles son las agencias que hay detrás de los principales futbolistas? El Informe del CIES (Centro Internacional de Estudios del Deporte), publicado en abril de 2026, recoge el ranking de las agencias de fútbol más poderosas según el valor estimado de transferencias de los jugadores representados. La número 1 es ‘CAA Stellar’ (2.560 millones de euros), agencia de jugadores como Elliot Anderson, Fermín o Camavinga. En el puesto número 2 está ‘Gestifute’ (1.860 M€), la empresa de Mendes, con Lamine, Vitinha y Mourinho como cabezas visibles. Completando el podio se encuentra ‘The.Team’ (1.250 M€), agencia de Federico Valverde, Grimaldo o Manzambi. En el cuarto lugar está ‘Unique Sports Group’ (1.110 M€), empresa que representa a Gordon o Guéhi. En mitad de la tabla aparece ‘Roof Uta & Klutch Sports Group’ (820 M€), agencia de Lookman o Havertz. El puesto número 6 es para ‘As 1 Sports’ (710 M€), con Nuno Mendes, Luis Díaz y Bruno Fernandes como principales activos. En el 7 está ‘Roc Nation’ (670 M€), donde destacan Vinicius, Endrick y Diomande. En el top 8 aparece ‘Sports Entertainment Group’ (620 M€), con Gakpo y Guardiola como estrellas. En el penúltimo lugar de la lista se encuentra ‘Bertolucci Assessoria’ (590 M€), agencia de Gabriel, Bruno Guimaraes o Matheus Cunha. El ranking lo cierra ‘MS Foot’ (530 M€), con Dembélé a la cabeza. No obstante, en MARCA hemos querido ir más allá de dicha clasificación y hablar con algunas de estas agencias para saber cuál es su trabajo, su relación con el jugador, cómo actúan en términos de fichajes y con qué criterios establecen sus ‘famosas’ comisiones. La génesis de este desconocido decorado surge en el proceso de captación. Y es que sí, además de en el que se sumergen cada verano o enero, las agencias de representación tienen su propio mercado de fichajes. De ello habla Cristian Pérez, agente de Sports Entertainment Group (SEG), agencia ‘top 8’ mundial según el CIES: “La primera toma de contacto siempre la hacemos para explorar la posibilidad y el estatus del jugador. Si el jugador en ese momento está feliz y contento con el trabajo que está haciendo su agente, nosotros ya lo descartamos. Si creemos que hay alguna posibilidad le explicamos cuál es nuestro proyecto, nuestra forma de trabajar, qué le podemos ofrecer o en qué mercados le podemos dar visibilidad”. Asimismo, existe el caso contrario, en el que el jugador acude a la agencia de representación, tal y como cuenta Rodolfo Orife, de Gersh. Esta agencia ha crecido en gran medida tras la adquisición de YouFirst, que ya en 2022 fue incluida por Forbes en el ‘top 10’ de agencias deportivas más valiosas del mundo. Entre sus filas tienen a personalidades de la talla de agencia de Luis de la Fuente, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Fabián Ruiz o Alexia Putellas, y cuenta con un valor de 838,24 millones de euros según Transfermarkt. “Es gratificante ayudar a futbolistas como Fabián con el que empezamos a trabajar hace más de 10 años, y acompañarlo en este proceso hasta convertirse en Campeón del Mundo, Eurocopa, dos Champions League consecutivas, candidato al Balón de Oro, etc. Después de tantos años y por nuestra manera de trabajar, en ocasiones son incluso los futbolistas los que se ponen en contacto con nosotros para que los representemos”, desvela Rodolfo Orife. En este paradigma, añade Thiago Freitas, director de operaciones de Roc Nation, influye mucho la etapa del jugador en cuestión: “Todo depende de la edad, del sitio en el que está el jugador, del nivel y perspectivas que tiene este jugador. Nosotros captamos por referencias de otras personas a través de nuestro proceso de scouting, por la observación que se hace de vídeos, por contactos que se dan por las redes sociales. Luego, otras veces, lo hacemos por medio de personas que trabajan en los clubes y hacen un diagnóstico de que un chico necesita algo más, que el club no puede ofrecer, y por eso llegan a nosotros. Son diferentes maneras de aproximarse a un jugador, pero lo que buscamos siempre es seguridad y firmeza”. No obstante, la vorágine de este mercado también puede llevar a situaciones complejas, señala Antonio Sanz, director de comunicación de Bahía Internacional (agencia de representación de Mikel Merino y Pau Cubarsí, entre muchos otros): “Hay una competencia desleal en la profesión de agente. No se respetan los acuerdos. Los jugadores suelen tener un acuerdo de una o dos temporadas contigo y en mitad de la temporada algunos jugadores, no todos, empiezan a escuchar a otros agentes. Los agentes se entrometen en la vida de tu jugador y tu empresa. En fin, hay una competencia feroz y, para mí, desleal en algunos puntos”. Todos consideran que las agencias de representación han evolucionado de forma cuantiosa en los últimos años. Hasta el punto en el que estas empresas se han convertido en multinacionales que ofrecen una gran variedad de servicios. “En Gersh tenemos un servicio 360, es decir, hay distintos departamentos para ayudar al jugador a mejorar su carrera. Tenemos un departamento legal, financiero, de comunicación, servicios, marketing, ‘player performance’, o sea, rendimiento deportivo, nutrición… Básicamente somos un equipo enorme dedicado a ayudar al futbolista para que el jugador se preocupe de lo que ocurre en el césped y poco más”, explica Rodolfo Orife. Ese abanico de servicios también está disponible para el agente, cuenta Cristian Pérez (SEG): “Disponemos de cualquier herramienta que puedas necesitar. Trabajamos con las mejores herramientas de big data, de análisis de jugadores y mercados para saber dónde encaja mejor un jugador determinado”. Thiago Freitas considera que el servicio más importante que ofrecen en Roc Nation es el de diagnóstico: “Procuramos mostrar a este jugador lo que es a la mirada de las personas que toman las decisiones en los clubes. Pero también les mostramos cómo eran los jugadores que hoy están en los grandes clubes a su edad”. Dentro de esas prestaciones se encuentra el trato con el jugador. Una relación que suele variar en función del deportista en cuestión. “Normalmente hablamos diariamente con el futbolista, sobre cómo ha ido el entrenamiento, cómo está, si está cargado o tiene alguna molestia”, señala Antonio Sanz, de Bahía Internacional. Igualmente, existen perfiles totalmente opuestos. “Hay deportistas que solo buscan un soporte cada 30 días sobre una compilación de todo lo que hizo en su club. Son gente con familia, mujer e hijos y tienen su propia vida”, apunta Thiago Freitas. Y en este apartado también entra la personalidad del agente, añade Cristian Pérez: “Yo para eso soy muy cercano, Yo necesito contacto constante con los jugadores, más que nada porque el componente emocional es clave en este negocio y saber lo que piensan en cada momento, lo que sienten, cuáles son sus expectativas, cómo quieren actuar en el próximo mercado, cómo se encuentra con su familia es clave. Al final siempre hablamos mucho de empresas, pero yo siempre digo que yo soy mucho más de personas”. La pregunta básica que nos solemos hacer en lo que a las agencias de representación se refiere es tan simple como compleja: ¿Cuál es su papel en una negociación? Así lo explica el propio Cristian, agente de SEG: “Por un lado, nuestro papel es intermediar entre los clubes para que lleguen a un acuerdo, porque la valoración que puede hacer el club de un jugador no tiene por qué ser la misma que hace el club de destino. Esta es una de las mayores guerras y situaciones más difíciles. Y luego, una vez se da este acuerdo, tratamos de conseguir las mejores condiciones económicas con nuestros clientes”. En ese tipo de negociaciones, es necesario encontrar el equilibrio digno de un funambulista para no tensar la cuerda hasta el punto que pueda romperse, y más en casos como las renovaciones: “Este asunto es el más complejo porque hay un componente emocional y de sentimiento de pertenencia con los clubes que entran en juego. Aquí ya no solo es la parte económica, es la parte personal. Es verdad que también importan el componente deportivo (el estatus que va a tener dentro del equipo ) y el económico, no vamos a ser hipócritas. Pero lo cierto es que si el jugador está contento y siente pertenencia con el club, seguramente acepte unas condiciones diferentes a las que aceptaría si no fuese así”. Pero estos acuerdos no siempre tienen un final feliz. “Si tensas la cuerda, la puedes romper. Te puede salir bien si cede la parte contraria o te puede salir mal y te quedas sin oferta. En muchas ocasiones ha habido jugadores que no han aceptado la oferta, se han puesto en el mercado, han visto que no le mejoraban ese contrato, y cuando han vuelto al club de origen les han dicho que la oferta había caducado”, confiesa Antonio Sanz (Bahía Internacional). Esto, puntualiza Cristian, puede pasar por la distinta valoración que hace el club en cuestión respecto a la agencia de representación o el jugador. O también, remarca Thiago Freitas, por la naturaleza del club en sí: “Esto ocurre especialmente en países que son exportadores de jugadores como Brasil”. No hay que irse muy lejos en el tiempo para ver que las renovaciones no son el único conflicto dentro del ‘mercato’. Suele ser habitual ver cada verano a jugadores que quieren salir de su club por diferentes motivos. Estas semanas el caso más sonado ha sido el de Julián. Existe el dicho de que los futbolistas juegan donde quieren, pero por algo es un dicho, y no una realidad. La pregunta es: ante esta situación, ¿qué puede hacer un agente? Thiago Freitas, director de operaciones de Roc Nation, lo tiene claro: “A largo plazo debemos trabajar para que el jugador esté siempre donde quiera estar, pero nunca sin respetar los contratos que tiene. El jugador debe buscar la vida que quiere, pero aún más debe dar su vida por el contrato que tiene. Muchas veces tenemos que dejar claro al jugador que en el momento que firma un contrato debe estar preparado para que las cosas no vayan bien y comprender que el interés de otro club no genera una obligación de que su actual club permita una salida”. Antonio Sanz recuerda el caso de Sergio Agüero, quien “quiso jugar en el Real Madrid y terminó jugando en el Manchester City”. Apunta que, en este tipo de contextos, desde Bahía Internacional les plantean una estrategia a los futbolistas, aunque “es el mercado el que te va marcando hacia dónde va la carrera de cada uno”. En todo caso, no cree que sea malo jugar donde uno quiere: “Es hasta es bueno. Si tú quieres jugar en el Real Madrid y tienes la oportunidad de jugar en el Real Madrid, ¿por qué no vas a jugar en el Real Madrid o en el Barcelona, o en el Athletic de Bilbao o en la Real Sociedad? Yo creo que el jugador cuanto más cerca está del equipo con el que sueña mejor jugador es”. Y es que, para Cristian Pérez (SEG), esta situación tampoco interesa al club: “No es interesante tener un jugador que conlleva un coste y que no está contento por cualquier motivo. Para el club conlleva un coste que no se va a reflejar en el campo, porque las situaciones anímicas van a hacer que no esté el 100%. Al final es mantener un equilibrio entre las condiciones que tienes firmadas con el club y lo que ello supone y el deseo del jugador”. Esta circunstancia es mucho más sencilla, añade Cristian, cuando el futbolista no tiene tiempo de juego o es el club el que decide venderlo. “En este caso se le pone en el mercado. Es decir, nosotros a partir de ese momento le buscamos posibles destinos. Cuando se habla de ‘mover al jugador’ quiere decir que su perfil está siendo hablado con muchos clubes y con muchos países en función de los gustos o del jugador en sí. Es muy habitual, sobre todo en verano, que es un mercado mucho más amplio, que ciertos clubes por situaciones de plantilla, por gustos de entrenador, o por situaciones económicas, no cuenten con un jugador en su planificación para el siguiente año y nos pidan buscar una salida”, desvela el agente de SEG. Para este tipo de casos una agencia internacional como SEG es fundamental, ya que cuentan con ramificaciones en todos los países: “Tenemos acceso a la totalidad de los equipos. Eso a nosotros nos facilita el trabajo un montón, en el sentido de que tienes acceso a clubes que, seguramente, por ti mismo sería mucho más difícil llegar y con relaciones seguramente más establecidas y de muchos más años que si yo personalmente hablo con un cierto club. Al final, ese es nuestro trabajo, buscar posibilidades para nuestros clientes. Hay veces que esas posibilidades aparecen en España, y otras veces que te tienes que ir a otro mercado importante de las cinco grandes o a un mercado más secundario”. Aquí ya no solo influyen las relaciones con otros agentes, sino también, los vínculos entre clubes y las preferencias que tienen estos por determinadas agencias o agentes: “No está bien decirlo, pero esto ocurre. En todos los clubes pasa que tienen cierta preferencia por ciertos agentes. No quiero decir que a otras agencias no les hagan caso o que no valoren sus jugadores, sino que seguramente en momentos de más necesidad la primera llamada va a ser a cierta agencia”. Ninguno habla de que haya agencias vetadas, porque ante situaciones de urgencia, cualquier solución es buena, pero Antonio Sanz, de Bahía Internacional, sí que habla de casos en los que un club intenta ir a por un jugador y una agencia negocia con ellos y acaba dando un giro de 180 grados y se lo llevan a otro club: “Es lógico que el primer club se enfade y se piense dos veces el trabajar contigo”. Asimismo, cada vez es más usual ver al agente como un intermediario entre clubes, además de como un representante de un determinado jugador. “Nosotros en SEG hemos intermediado en el fichaje de Baleba por el Manchester United, a pesar de no ser de nuestra agencia. Es otra parte de nuestro trabajo. El tener un nombre y tener una repercusión como agencia nos facilita llegar a este tipo de acuerdos con clubes”, desvela Cristian. Para finalizar este apartado, Thiago Freitas (Roc Nation) quiere desmitificar la leyenda de que los jugadores son controlados por sus agentes: “Eso no es verdad. Los agentes son contratados por los jugadores para la defensa de sus intereses”. Y no hay mayor mito o leyenda urbana en el mundo de la representación que el tema de las comisiones. Siempre se atribuyen grandes cantidades de dinero a los agentes, especialmente en operaciones de gran calado. Según el informe de Agentes de Fútbol de 2025 elaborado por la FIFA, el año pasado se repartieron 1.370 millones de dólares en comisiones totales a agentes, estableciendo un nuevo récord histórico y representando un aumento de más del 90 % en comparación con 2024, lo que refleja tanto una mayor actividad de traspasos como movimientos de jugadores de mayor valor. Lo que desconoce la gente es de dónde sale ese dinero. “El mayor mito que hay es que los agentes cobran de los traspasos. Nuestros honorarios los acordamos con nuestros futbolistas. Hay un error muy común y es que la gente piensa que cuanto mayor es el traspaso, más cobra el agente. En nuestro caso, de hecho, tratamos de abaratar los traspasos para conseguir mejor contrato a nuestros jugadores”, señala Loren del Pino, agente de GERSH. Los porcentajes en las comisiones varían en función de la agencia en cuestión, pero, entre todos, apuntan a que suele estar entre el 2 y el 10%. “Quien paga las comisiones a los agentes son los jugadores. Es parte de las cantidades que el club tiene para el jugador. Y es siempre importante recordar que ningún jugador en el mundo tiene la obligación legal de contratar a un agente. Los jugadores tienen agentes porque piensan que tener un agente es importante”, explica Thiago Freitas (Roc Nation). También depende, señala Cristian Pérez (SEG), de si se trata de un fichaje de un jugador que está libre o un traspaso habitual: “Ya nos gustaría a todos ganar esas cantidades que se piensa la gente que ganamos. Además, ser agente conlleva mucho trabajo detrás. Es decir, la comisión es el resultado, pero nadie se da cuenta de todo lo que hay entre el momento que se empieza a trabajar y que se consigue ese resultado. Son muchas horas sin dormir, mucha presión”. En cuanto al futuro de las agencias de representación y el fútbol, cada uno tiene su visión, aunque no distan mucho entre sí. La principal coincidencia de la que hablan es de la llegada de las grandes empresas. “Cada vez el agente pequeño va a tener más dificultades, sobre todo, porque al final sí que hace falta ese potencial económico para acceder a ciertos jugadores. Creo que la tecnología va a ser otra de las situaciones que se está desarrollando ya y que puede ser importante y tener impacto en los próximos años. Hay plataformas que ya actúan como intermediarios entre clubes, agencias, jugadores y que facilitan ciertos contactos. Es decir, nunca va a reemplazar a la actividad de un agente, pero sí que va a cambiar un poco las reglas de juego y cómo se actúa”, augura Cristián Pérez (SEG). Algo parecido a lo que espera Antonio Sanz, de Bahía Internacional: “Nosotros, además de que sean buenos jugadores, también buscamos buenas personas y creo que el objetivo que está marcado es seguir trabajando, seguir ayudando a los chicos a que crezcan, hacerles sentir importantes y hacerles dichosos con la profesión que han elegido. Respecto al ámbito de la representación creo que cada vez entrarán más fondos de inversión y compañías muy potentes”. En Gersh, buscarán “abrir mercados y tener más alcance”, para ello se apoyarán “dentro de la agencia, en aquellas personas que trabajan con nosotros para el futbolista en distintos departamentos: comunicación, departamento legal, servicios, marketing…”. Por último, Thiago Freitas (Roc Nation), nos deja un curioso vaticinio: “Es importante recordar que los jugadores no son productos. No son algo que se venda y se compra. Yo creo que con el tiempo, cada vez más, los jugadores se van a volver socios del dinero que los clubes generan y va a ser más interesante para los jugadores seguir donde están, especialmente en los grandes clubes. Los jugadores van a ser como los propietarios de las franquicias en Estados Unidos, parte también de la sociedad y eso va a cambiar todo en el fútbol”.

articles.title: Aubameyang, una pesadilla para el Valencia
articles.standfirst: Le hizo cuatro goles en una semifinal de Europa League (2019) y firmó su único hat-trick en la Liga en Mestalla (2022)
articles.summary: Le hizo cuatro goles en una semifinal de Europa League (2019) y firmó su único hat-trick en la Liga en Mestalla (2022)
articles.body: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ha arrancado LaLiga 2026/27 como acostumbra a hacerlo un goleador nato: marcando. El veterano delantero del Deportivo suma dos tantos en sus dos primeros partidos con el conjunto gallego y vuelve a dejar claro que conserva intacto el instinto que le convirtió en una referencia europea durante más de una década. En Valencia, además, su nombre despierta recuerdos especialmente desagradables. Los tres goles que anotó al conjunto de Mestalla en LaLiga representan su mejor registro frente a un mismo rival en la competición. Todos llegaron en una tarde para el olvido del valencianismo: el 20 de febrero de 2022, cuando firmó el único hat trick de su carrera en la Liga española durante la victoria del Barcelona por 1-4 en Mestalla. El entonces fichaje invernal de Xavi Hernández marcó dos tantos en la primera parte y terminó llevándose también el cuarto gol barcelonista, inicialmente atribuido a Pedri pero concedido después por el árbitro en el acta al gabonés al desviar el balón en su trayectoria hacia la portería. Pero el inicio de la pesadilla se encuentra algunas temporadas atrás. Aubameyang fue el gran verdugo del Valencia en las semifinales de la Europa League 2018/19. Marcó y asistió en el triunfo del Arsenal por 3-1 en Londres y repitió con otro triplete en el 2-4 de Mestalla que certificó la eliminación valencianista y el pase de los ingleses a la final. El balance global es demoledor. Contra el Valencia, Aubameyang ha participado en cuatro partidos oficiales, con un saldo de tres victorias y un empate, siete goles y una asistencia. Ningún otro rival parece despertar de forma tan clara la mejor versión del delantero gabonés. Ahora, con el Deportivo de regreso a Primera y Aubameyang nuevamente enchufado, el Valencia vuelve a tener motivos para vigilar a uno de los atacantes que más daño le ha causado en el siglo XXI. Entre Europa y LaLiga, el nombre del gabonés ya ocupa un lugar incómodo en la memoria reciente de Mestalla.
