articles.title: Grecia es una mina: “Son el futuro del país”
articles.standfirst: Ha habido 20 traspasos de jugadores griegos este verano y han movido cerca de 160 millones de euros • No acuden a un gran torneo de selecciones desde el Mundial 2014
articles.summary: Ha habido 20 traspasos de jugadores griegos este verano y han movido cerca de 160 millones de euros • No acuden a un gran torneo de selecciones desde el Mundial 2014
articles.body: Grecia es uno de los destinos turísticos por excelencia a nivel Mundial. Los ingresos superan los 20.000 millones de euros anuales, lo que supone alrededor de un 19% del PIB del país, y los 30 millones de turistas que suelen albergar de media generan unos 800.000 puestos de trabajo. Una auténtica mina de generar dinero que, en los últimos años, también están sabiendo trasladar al mundo del fútbol a la hora de crear y exportar talento. A menos de dos semanas para que cierre el mercado, hay un total de 20 jugadores griegos que han movido dinero en materia de traspasos y el montante total asciende hasta cerca de los 160 millones de euros. Unos 55 más en relación a la temporada anterior… donde se movieron hasta 34 futbolistas griegos. En consecuencia, cuatro de los 10 fichajes griegos más caros de la historia se han producido durante esta ventana estival. El más caro de todos, habiendo desbancado a Kostas Manolas de la primera posición, ha sido un Christos Tzolis por el que el Arsenal ha desembolsado 40 millones de euros tras ser elegido como mejor jugador de la Jupiler Pro League el curso pasado. Fue, sin duda, la gran estrella del campeonato belga y sus 40 goles generados en Liga tuvieron buena parte de culpa en la reconquista del título por parte del Brujas. “Está entrando en el equipo de una forma realmente orgánica”, dijo Mikel Arteta tras la Community Shield, donde arrancó como titular en banda izquierda y presentó su candidatura a hacerse con el puesto repartiendo sus dos primeras asistencias. “Es muy inteligente y tiene una cualidad enorme en los últimos 20 o 30 metros para encontrar a sus compañeros u generar ocasiones. Hoy lo ha demostrado”. Otro ‘gigante’ como el Borussia Dortmund ha ‘pescado’ a otras dos de las grandes 'joyas' del fútbol griego para su mediapunta. Primero, se dejaron 30 millones en Karetsas, goleador más joven en la historia del país y segundo máximo asistente (11) de la Liga belga con el Genk sólo por detrás, precisamente, de Tzolis. Desde el PAOK, generando un auténtico cisma con la afición, han reclutado a Konstantelias a cambio de 26 millones. Jugadores griegos más caros de la historia: De aquí, además de Tzolis, también salió un Koulierakis que, previo paso por el Wolfsburgo, ha recalado en la Roma por 16.5 millones. No son los únicos: Stefanos Tzimas, dos años atrás, puso rumbo al Nüremberg por 22 ‘kilos’ para, de inmediato, firmar por el Brighton a cambio de 26.5 millones. En el AMEX, por cierto, se juega el puesto en punta de ataque con otro griego como Charalampos Kostoulas por quien Olympiacos ingresó 35 millones hace justo un año. Hasta 23.3 millones también han ganado con la venta de Tzolakis a un Hull City recién ascendido a Premier. Algo más, 23.6 millones para ser exactos, pagó el Newcastle hace unos años por Vlachodimos, su principal competencia en la portería de una Grecia que, poco a poco, ha ido generando futbolistas de cierto renombre en todas las líneas del terreno de juego. Además de todos estos jugadores, también cuentan con Pavlidis (Benfica), Douvikas (Como), Mouzakitis (Olympiacos), Mavropanos (West Ham), Ioannidis (Sporting), Mandas (Lazio), Vagiannidis (Sporting)… “Estos jugadores son el futuro del fútbol griego y, por nuestra parte, debemos darles todas las oportunidades para que, a través de las experiencias que adquieran y de la colaboración con jugadores más experimentados, tengan la oportunidad de representar al país en los próximos años”, expuso Ivan Jovanovic, seleccionador nacional, en el parón de selecciones de marzo. La gesta lograda en 2004 es irrepetible. Pero, desde luego, hay mimbres para intentar volver a clasificar a un gran torneo de selecciones. Su última Eurocopa se remonta a la edición de 2012 y no pisan por un Mundial desde 2014. Para este último, de hecho, no se metieron ni en la ‘repesca’. Es momento, por tanto, para volver a poner a Grecia en el mapa a nivel futbolístico y la Nations League, donde comparten grupo con Alemania, Países Bajos y Serbia, será una buena piedra de toque para esta nueva generación.

articles.title: Flávio Gonçalves, el ‘cachorro’ que está revolucionando Portugal: “Es un chaval predestinado”
articles.standfirst: El talentoso mediapunta luso, de origen francés, ha sido titular con el Sporting CP en las cuatro primeras jornadas y ya ha generado tres goles
articles.summary: El talentoso mediapunta luso, de origen francés, ha sido titular con el Sporting CP en las cuatro primeras jornadas y ya ha generado tres goles
articles.body: El Sporting CP siempre se ha caracterizado por ser una de las mejores ‘fábricas’ del mundo a la hora de generar atacantes de élite: Luis Figo, Cristiano Ronaldo, Ricardo Quaresma, Simao, Nani, Rafa Leao… El último que hizo las maletas rumbo al Chelsea por 50 millones fue Geovany Quenda… y el siguiente podría ser un Flávio Gonçalves (Mantes-la-Jolie, 2007) que está siendo la gran apuesta de Rui Borges en este inicio de curso. Nacido en Francia, aunque internacional con Portugal en categoría Sub18 (13), Sub19 (12) y Sub20 (cuatro), se incorporó a la academia del Sporting CP procedente del Rio Ave en 2019 con apenas 12 años. Su ascenso por las categorías inferiores le permitió irse saltando bastantes pasos... hasta conseguir asomar la cabeza por el primer equipo la temporada pasada. Debutó en octubre contra el Alverca en Taça da Liga sustituyendo al propio Quenda y firmó su primera asistencia en favor de Salvador Blopa, canterano de su misma quinta. “Flávio ha tenido un crecimiento muy bueno en el equipo 'B'. Ha respondido y madurado. Se nota que es un chaval atrevido con el balón, no se esconde y tiene un futuro muy prometedor si sigue trabajando de la misma manera que lo ha hecho hasta ahora”, reconoció aquel día un Rui Borges que le dio la oportunidad de disputar siete partidos con el primer equipo. “Trabajé para poder cumplir el sueño de debutar en el Alvalade”, comentó Flávio Gonçalves en sus redes sociales. Durante la pretemporada, sin embargo, terminó de derribar la puerta del Sporting CP... hasta el punto de haber arrancado como titular en las cuatro primeras jornadas de la Primeira Liga 26-27. Especialmente emotivo fue el duelo contra Vitória Guimaraes en el que fue capaz de anotar su primer gol. “Es una sensación inexplicable. Me gustaría dedicárselo a todas las personas de la academia que lo hicieron todo por mí”. Está yendo a más con el paso de los partidos. En la goleada ante Rio Ave, su club de origen, se lució abriendo el marcador a pase de Issa Doumbia con un disparo sutil al palo largo tras dibujarle un gran desmarque entre central y lateral; y le regaló una asistencia de ‘trivela’ a Geny Catamo en el 0-2. “Fue mi primera casa. Empecé aquí y tengo mucho respeto por el Rio Ave. Me ayudaron mucho cuando llegué de Francia”, dijo después del partido. Con permiso de Luis Suárez, que anotó un doblete, fue el gran protagonista de la noche. Rui Borges, sin embargo, le exige todavía más. “Está creciendo. Al contrario que ustedes, a mí no me gustó. Falló muchos pases. Es un chaval predestinado, con una calidad muy por encima de la media. Estoy de broma, claro que me gustó su partido. Pero puede mejorar”, matizó. A pesar de formarse como ‘10’ en categorías inferiores, Rui Borges lo está ‘acostando’ a la banda izquierda... aunque goza con plena libertad de movimientos. “No me importa dónde jugar: izquierda, derecha... No tengo preferencia”, dice. Es un jugador muy pulcro técnicamente al que le gusta recibir al pie y meterse al carril central para ‘mediapuntear’. Derrocha creatividad en el último tercio, tiene toques de genio y está mezclando de maravilla con un perfil de lateral tan profundo como Maxi Araújo. Con un 60% de éxito, es el tercer jugador del Sporting CP que más regates promedia (0.8) y, además, también el segundo que más remata (2.0). “Tenemos características parecidas y es un jugador al que admiro mucho”, reconocía tiempo atrás Flávio Gonçalves sobre su compatriota ‘Pote’... al que ahora está ‘atropellando’. Obviamente, la muestra es bastante pequeña todavía. A sus 19 años, apenas suma 11 partidos con el primer equipo de un Sporting CP que, eso sí, ya se encargó de blindarlo hasta 2030. Rui Borges, incluso, le recomienda “no emocionarse enseguida”. De momento, ya ha generado tres goles y se ha convertido en el nuevo ‘cachorro’ de moda en Portugal.

articles.title: El único gol del defensa elegante
articles.standfirst: Clemente Fernández resolvió a favor del Madrid la primera visita del Málaga en Primera a Chamartín
articles.summary: Clemente Fernández resolvió a favor del Madrid la primera visita del Málaga en Primera a Chamartín
articles.body: El Málaga regresa esta tarde a Chamartín. Después de casi nueve años, el equipo de la capital de la Costa del Sol regresa a una casa, la del Real Madrid, en la que nunca ha ganado un partido de Liga. La cuenta se coloca en 38 con un balance hasta hoy de 30 triunfos madridistas y siete empates. Esa rivalidad liguera en el templo blanco se abrió el 12 de febrero de 1950. El Madrid llegaba en crisis: cuatro partidos sin ganar, goleado la semana anterior en el Metropolitano por 5-1 y sólo dos triunfos en las once últimas jornadas. Una pésima racha que no sacó al Madrid de la pelea por una Liga que se vestiría de rojiblanco madrileño, la tercera para los atléticos y la primera conquistada en su estadio. Atascado en juego y resultados, el partido ante el Málaga también se le atragantó al equipo de Mr. Keeping, cuyo rival en el banquillo andaluz era una leyenda del Madrid y de España: Ricardo Zamora. A falta de solo cinco minutos, el marcador estaba en empate a uno, la gente de uñas y la sombra de otro partido sin ganar amenazaba al Madrid. Entonces, Molowny sacó una falta y Clemente Fernández, central madridista, enganchó un duro remate a la red. “Vi venir la pelota y no lo dudé”, contaba el goleador. Por su parte, el portero del Málaga, Césareo López, se quejaba: “Ha sido una falta clarísima antes del remate, de Pahíño a Aranau”. Era el primer gol de Clemente con el Madrid. Y el único que marcó en sus once temporadas en la Casa Blanca y sus 213 partidos (144 oficiales). En una época de defensas rudos y para quienes la pelota era un objeto a alejar, Clemente destacaba por su buen trato de balón y su capacidad para interpretar el juego desde atrás. Un central en una era equivocada. Había un porqué detrás. Fue en el madrileño Paseo de Extremadura donde Clemente se hizo futbolista. Nació el 23 de noviembre de 1919, los primeros pasos los dio en la Unión de Amigos del Deporte. Era capitán, fundador, financiador con 25 céntimos de peseta a la semana... y delantero centro. Porque su ídolo y referente era Gaspar Rubio. Su juego, en el que fue retrasando posiciones, se hizo popular. Recorrió varios equipos antes de llegar al Madrid, que se lo llevó desde el Betis de Cuatro Caminos. El 26 de abril de 1942 debutó de blanco: 1-3 en el campo de la Ferroviaria. En Chamartín hacía meses que se le seguía la pista. Pero la decisión de fichar a Clemente se aceleró a las puertas del arranque de la Copa de 1942. Las lesiones de Mardones y Arzanegui precipitaron los hechos. Un contrato por cinco mil pesetas fue el primer vínculo entre el madrileño y el equipo con el que ganaría dos veces la Copa y otra el embrión de la Supercopa, la Copa Eva Duarte. Tenía Clemente 22 años al llegar al Madrid. En la temporada siguiente jugó tres partidos de Liga. Su debut fue en San Mamés, en noviembre de 1942. Fue una derrota por 3-2 en la que se enfrentó por primera vez al delantero que siempre identificó como el más complicado de sujetar: Piru Gainza. Entre sus compañeros, Clemente destacaba la clase que poseía Ipiña. A pesar de que jugó poco, el Madrid creía en él. La decisión fue cederlo al Hércules. En Alicante jugó 25 de los 26 partidos de Liga en Segunda. La temporada no fue buena para un equipo que aspiraba al ascenso, pero sí para Clemente. Los buenos informes se acumularon en Chamartín. El 3 de julio de 1944 fue despedido a lo grande como jugador del Hércules. Fue en el viejo estadio de Bardín en la final de la Copa de la Región que se quedó en casa al vencer 2-1 al Elche. Apenas dos semanas más tarde, Clemente volvía a jugar con el Madrid. El 16 de julio, el equipo blanco abría su pretemporada con un triunfo en Melilla: 2-3. Era la primera piedra de un largo camino que se clausuró el 30 de noviembre de 1952, con un amistoso en Chamartín ante el Jaén (6-1). Después del Madrid jugó una temporada en el Deportivo. Fue internacional tres veces, todas como madridista. El 17 de julio de 1996 murió en Madrid sin rastro en la prensa de la desaparición del central del que su mujer, Mari Tere, contaba que se enfadaba poco, pero si le despertaban de la siesta...

articles.title: La hora del 'hijo' Rüdiger
articles.standfirst: El único jugador de campo sano de la primera plantilla que no se ha estrenado
articles.summary: El único jugador de campo sano de la primera plantilla que no se ha estrenado
articles.body: "Vamos a pensar en el Mundial y después me voy con mi padre". Esa fue la respuesta de Antonio Rüdiger en plena Copa del Mundo al ser preguntado por cómo imaginaba al nuevo Madrid, que quedaba en manos de Jose Mourinho. Eliminada Alemania en el primer cruce, en los penaltis ante Paraguay, Rüdiger se fue pronto de vacaciones. Eso le permitió estar desde el inicio en los planes de trabajo de Mourinho. Pero, a las puertas de la tercera jornada de Liga, es el único jugador de campo, al margen de los siete lesionados, que aún no ha tenido minutos Consciente de la importancia de empezar con paso firme, el entrenador portugués ha querido que el centro de su zaga sea una zona de fortaleza. Por eso, Konaté y Huijsen forman parte del quinteto de jugadores que suman los 180 minutos que van de Liga. Los otros son Courtois, Valverde y Mbappé. Por ello, el berlinés es uno de los jugadores que cotizan más alto de cara al once ante el Málaga. Después de repetir equipo en las dos primeras jornadas, el plan de Mourinho pasa por abrir puertas en el once y Rüdiger está bien colocado para estrenarse en el campeonato. Tener a Rüdiger sin jugar es una decisión de poco riesgo. El alemán es un soldado, uno de esos jugadores que son oro para un entrenador y para el día a día de un vestuario. En el Madrid desde el verano de 2022, se ha convertido en una de las voces más autorizadas en la caseta blanca. No necesita ser un intocable para que, cuando habla, se sepa que lo hace un mando. Tras una temporada cargada de problemas físicos, Rüdiger, que en marzo cumple 34 años, tuvo muchas dudas a la hora de renovar. Pero lo hizo, en gran parte porque para Mourinho es un seguro de vida tener a alguien de su personalidad en el equipo. Habituado a estar por encima de los 40 partidos por temporada, la pasada solo pudo aparecer en 26. Una cifra tan baja no la conocía desde la temporada 2014-15, cuando disputó 22 con el Stuttgart. La pasada fue una campaña en la que no fue capaz de escapar de las lesiones. Eso se convirtió en un problema de magnitud en el Madrid, porque se sumaba a las lesiones de Militao, un Alaba fuera de la élite, el bajón tremendo que sufrió Huijsen y la desaparición de Asencio. Reforzada la posición de central con Konaté, tener a un Rüdiger al nivel que ha sido habitual desde que llegó al Madrid sería una excelente noticia para Mourinho. De momento, debe dar los primeros pasos y sumar los primeros minutos oficiales. El entrenador portugués sabe que tiene a un soldado en el alemán, alguien de quien se puede fiar como si fuera su hijo.

articles.title: Samba Stars: Michail Antonio helps Ghanaian academy chase Premier League dreams
articles.summary: Former West Ham forward Michail Antonio is helping players from a Ghana academy, who have travelled to England in the hope of turning pro.
articles.body:
In the heat of rural Leicestershire, the Samba Stars are chasing their dream.

Head coach Freddie Okyere has just finished a shooting exercise and allows the squad to catch their breath.

The teenagers from the Ghanaian academy, which is backed by former West Ham and Nottingham Forest forward Michail Antonio, have spent two and a half months in England with one goal - impressing clubs and earning a contract.

While scouts do visit west Africa, it is rare for academies to travel to the UK to put their players directly in front of professional clubs.

"The talent the lads have is incredible," said Antonio.

"We created Samba Stars Academy to give young players in Ghana access to elite coaching, shape them as players and create real avenues into the pro game and show how much talent Ghana has."

Based in Kumasi while building a new facility in Bompata, just over 100 miles north of Ghana's capital Accra, the Samba Stars' tactic has paid off.

Bournemouth, Everton, Manchester City, Charlton, Preston, Barnsley and Peterborough have all taken players on trial this summer.

"The first two or three weeks it hadn't sunk in, but then they saw the facilities we'd be [using] and the teams we were playing," said Okyere.

"They want to go and show what they can do. They are hungry, they really want it. I'm hoping there will be so much interest because we have so much talent here.

"With the facilities we will have in Ghana we feel we will be top two, top three [academies]. We hope we can bring the best of Ghana to Europe."

There are other success stories, with midfielder Listowell Lord Hinneh joining Middlesbrough in February after a trial. , external

The 18-year-old has trained with the first team after swapping west Africa for England's north east.

"When I came in January, it was so cold. Experiencing something like that for the first time was tough," he told BBC Sport.

"Moving was a big milestone. It just makes me feel the dreams I've been having, thinking of trying to find myself in Europe to become a professional footballer.

"I feel the kind of dreams that I want, I'm on the verge. I'm on the way [to] becoming who I wanted to become."

Hinneh - whose sister Groovy lives in Leeds - met with the Samba Stars squad on their trip, offering advice.

"[I told them] what you've been dreaming about the future, it starts from here," he said.

"Don't just try, be so passionate. You need to play and enjoy it because you can have the success in whatever you're doing. You have to just put your heart in it."

'I'm seeing a different side of professional football'

All but one of the 20-strong visiting group initially had their visa application denied before eventually being admitted after re-evaluation.

Since arriving in the UK, they have been hosted by Brook House College in Market Harborough and trained at Harborough Town, who play in the National League North.

"The football [here] is very detailed," said 17-year-old goalkeeper Joshua Tetteh Tuwor.

"In Ghana we have the same passion but I'm seeing a different side of professional football.

"We are grateful to have such opportunities to train with elite coaches."

Rob Newman, formerly West Ham's head of recruitment and Manchester City's international scouting and recruitment manager, spent time with the academy in Ghana earlier this year and has helped coach them in Harborough.

"Hopefully clubs can see the potential," said the ex-Bristol City and Norwich defender.

"Nothing will give me greater pleasure in six months [than] going to see these boys playing in a first team in Europe. I believe they are two or three months away from being able to do that."

The Stars have played a series of games against youth teams from the EFL and non-league.

They started with a 9-0 thumping of Dorking Wanderers and also beat Under-21 sides from Sheffield Wednesday, Luton and Peterborough.

There were draws at Sheffield United and Barnsley while their only defeat came 3-2 against Preston's U21s.

Antonio watched them thrash Peterborough U19s 6-0 last month.

"You can see from what they've done since they've been in the UK - the results against top teams - that they have what it takes to play pro level," said the 36-year-old.

"It's great to help knock down barriers and give these lads a real chance."

'Back home everyone is depending on you'

Ghana have reached five of the past six Fifa World Cups - having never qualified before 2006 - and made the quarter-finals in 2010.

At this year's tournament, where they exited in the last-32 against Colombia, eight members of the squad were born overseas.

The Black Stars may not have come to rely heavily on diaspora talent, unlike some other African nations, yet the Ghana Football Association has made noises about widening its global search - something which could potentially impact home-grown talent.

"You have to have a tough mentality," said Sherif Mashud, an 18-year-old striker who has already had a trial with Hungarian top-tier side Zalaegerszegi thanks to his involvement with Samba Stars.

"Back home everyone is depending on you, everyone is looking up to you to succeed, to come and help them, your friends, your family. Everyone is praying for you."

The new English season has begun with six Ghana internationals on Premier League books: Mohammed Kudus at Tottenham, Antoine Semenyo with Manchester City, Brighton's Ibrahim Osman, Ipswich's new signing Abdul Fatawu and Coventry's Brandon Thomas-Asante and Caleb Yirenkyi.

The first to play in the English top flight was striker Nii Lamptey when he joined Aston Villa in 1994, while midfielder Michael Essien has made the most appearances, winning two titles with Chelsea.

Only two other Ghanaians have lifted the Premier League trophy - Jeffrey Schlupp and Daniel Amartey when Leicester stunned the world in 2015-16.

"Back home we've got people you grew up with and you might miss them, but that doesn't kill the dreams I'm here for," said Hinneh, who lists Kudus as his biggest inspiration and hopes to follow his heroes into the top flight after Boro missed out on promotion in last season's Championship play-off final.

"I'm trying to figure out what the reality is, what the future holds for me and then just chase the dreams."

articles.title: Messi scores four goals, inspires Inter Miami to 7-1 win over Montreal
articles.summary: Lionel Messi’s four goals help Miami snap a five-match winless run and take his season MLS tally to 18 goals.
articles.body:
Inter Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos ran out of superlatives for Lionel Messi after the Argentinian playmaker scored four goals in a Major League Soccer (MLS) match for the first time in his career to inspire a 7-1 thrashing of CF Montreal.

Messi’s four-goal haul and an assist on Saturday came at a crucial time for Miami, helping them snap a five-game winless run across all competitions.

The 39-year-old restored Miami’s advantage shortly before half-time, struck again in the 52nd minute, completed his hat-trick in the 83rd and capped his dazzling display with a free kick in stoppage time.

The former Barcelona forward now tops the MLS scoring charts with 18 goals this season.

“There are no words to describe such footballing beauty,” Argentinian Hoyos said. “So much is going on that words simply fall short.

“He is constantly looking for that goal, that play, that pass; I don’t think he’s an ordinary footballer. Analysing him, both as a player and as a person, goes so deep that you run out of words.”

Messi, who won the 2022 World Cup, also captained Argentina to this year’s World Cup final, where they lost to Spain .

“That’s what it means to have Messi on the team,” Miami midfielder Casemiro told Apple TV.

“We have to enjoy these moments because he is a person, a player that makes history.”

Casemiro, 34, joined Miami in July after his contract expired at Manchester United.

The Brazilian and Messi spent years on opposite sides of one of football’s fiercest rivalries, with Casemiro starring for Real Madrid and Messi for Barcelona, but are now teammates.

“We saw today that we have to enjoy it, keep supporting and keep competing with him because he continues to be the best,” Casemiro added.

“He proved it in the World Cup. We have to enjoy it because, with him, we are so much stronger.”

articles.summary: Después de la primera jornada visitará a Union Saint-Gilloise y Lillestrom y antes de la última recibirá a Torreense y Viktoria Plzen, partidos en los que deberá sacar muchos puntos
articles.body: La Real Sociedad comenzará la fase Liga de la Europa League recibiendo en Anoeta al Bournemouth y la concluirá visitando a la Juventus en Turín, dos de las citas más difíciles de las ocho que tendrá que acometer con el objetivo de clasificarse para los octavos de final o, al menos, la para le eliminatoria de clasificación. articles.body:
Real Madrid's start to life at the Santiago Bernabeu for the new season could not have gone any better as they destroyed Real Sociedad by a 4-1 scoreline in their first game in front of home fans.

Later today, they play their second consecutive clash at home, this time in an earlier kickoff against Malaga .

The newly promoted side have had a mixed start to life in the first division, losing to Atletico Madrid on Matchday 1 but salvaging a 1-1 draw against Deportivo de A Coruna in their subsequent game.

Needless to say, however, Real Madrid pose their biggest challenge yet, and it is safe to say that Jose Mourinho's men will be the overwhelming favourites coming into the game.

Madrid Universal brings you three talking points ahead of Real Madrid vs Malaga.

Marc Cucurella's announcement as a new Real Madrid player just before Spain's curtain-raiser at the FIFA World Cup came as a surprise to many, and the player's performances at the event made him a hugely hyped arrival.

Taking to the field for La Roja , the left-back was consistently one of the best players on the field for his nation and finished the tournament as a pillar of Luis de La Fuente's side.

Arriving at Real Madrid off the back of such a stellar event, needless to say, made it clear that he would be the undisputed starter at left-back under Jose Mourinho.

The first two games of the season, however, have not followed suit as the manager has preferred Alvaro Carreras over Cucurella.

While that might suggest that the manager rates the former more than the World Cup winner, it is more likely that he was gradually phasing the new signing in considering how he returned late to pre-season.

Now heading into the third game of the campaign, it is high time Cucurella enters the starting lineup, with the manager confirming that to be the case during his press conference.

So far, the new signing has been solid in all his appearances and has left a good impression, arriving at a new club. It will be interesting to see how he fares on his first start for Real Madrid.

Real Madrid turned on the style in the second half vs Sociedad. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

One of the biggest takeaways from Real Madrid's win over Real Sociedad midweek was how the men in white turned their situation completely around in the second half.

While they were in the driving seat throughout, the first half saw a far more balanced game with even the visitors creating their fair share of chances.

After the break, however, it was one-way traffic as Real Madrid dominated, created chances and even finished them with conviction. What changed was the combination play and improved understanding between the big three up front.

Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr. have all started the new season strongly, with the Frenchman and Englishman particularly looking in imperious form.

What has been lacking, however, is the understanding between the trio and the acceptance to play for the team and not individual accolades.

In the second half against La Real , Real Madrid finally played with a sense of long-lost selflessness and the trio began combining wonderfully. The buildup flowed without any hindrance and the result followed suit.

Later today, the effort must remain the same. If Real Madrid can continue operating on the same bandwidth and maintain that consistency, there will simply be no stopping them.

While Real Madrid may well have won both their games so far in La Liga, there is a clear sense that certain departments must improve.

One department that Jose Mourinho has marked in red , on that front, is the defence where Los Blancos have continued to look relatively shaky.

In both of the team's games so far, Real Madrid have failed to maintain a clean sheet and the defence has been sliced open quite easily. Surprisingly, they conceded shortly after taking the lead on both nights.

The lapses in concentration, needless to say, are simply not acceptable, more so in a team led by Mourinho where the defence is the heart of the team's success.

Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen have been the manager's preferred centre-halves so far this season, and all signs point to them continuing in that position. However, every game at this point is a test where they must show conspicuous improvement.

Concurrently, there will be more emphasis on improving the overall defensive output and working as a collective unit on that front. That too will remain a point of focus as the men in white grace the field for the third time in the new season.

Keeping a clean sheet, needless to say, will be an unsaid objective for the team as a whole, with special emphasis on the double-pivot and defence.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola: The 'grasshopper' whose family helped him reach the top
articles.summary: As Liverpool agree a £123m deal for Bradley Barcola, BBC Sport looks at how he has ridden triumphs and setbacks to reach the top with the help of his family.
articles.body:
There was a moment, not so long ago, when Bradley Barcola's career appeared to have stalled.

Having earned rave reviews after nailing down a regular starting place in Lyon's starting XI under Peter Bosz, the 20-year-old winger was out of favour and in the reserves by the time the Dutch coach was replaced by Laurent Blanc in October 2022.

According to L'Equipe, , external Barcola was close to joining Swiss club St Gallen in January 2023 in order to get more game time before an act of petulance by a team-mate helped pave his return to the side.

Fans were unhappy with the team's poor form - making first-choice forward Karl Toko Ekambi a target for their frustrations.

The relationship between the Cameroon international and Lyon's ultras fractured further when he stormed down the tunnel and kicked a rubbish bin in frustration after being substituted during a 2-1 home defeat by Strasbourg.

The incident was caught on camera and Toko Ekambi never played for Lyon again.

That presented Barcola with an opportunity which he seized. He started the majority of the remaining matches that season, scoring five times, including a winner at champions-in-waiting Paris St-Germain in April 2023.

Five months after that goal at the Parc des Princes, Barcola was a PSG player.

His reported £38.5m move - two weeks after Brazil forward Neymar swapped Paris for Saudi Arabia - came with Lyon struggling in the table and also unable to sign replacements because of financial restrictions.

"Barcola's first game for PSG was back at Lyon," Pierre-Etienne Minonzio, football journalist for L'Equipe, told BBC Sport.

"He was booed by the Lyon fans because it was just after the transfer. PSG boss Luis Enrique asked Barcola, who was very young at the time, if he was ready to play.

"He said yes, came on as a substitute, and it was impressive."

Barcola, nicknamed the 'grasshopper' because of his speed, agility and slight frame, has since gone on to win three Ligue 1 titles and back-to-back Champions Leagues in his three seasons in the French capital. He broke into the France side two years ago, and scored three times as this summer's World Cup as they reached the semi-finals.

With Liverpool agreeing a £123m deal to sign him, Barcola is on his way to the Premier League.

It has been quite the journey from kicking a ball about as a schoolboy on the playing fields of Vaulx-en-Velin - situated to the east of Lyon - to becoming a superstar worth nine figures. But the path has not been without challenges.

"Barcola is hugely ambitious," added Minonzio.

"He is from a generation of young French talent who are prepared to work hard and want to be a better version of themselves.

"They will do whatever they have to do to get there. They don't ask questions - they just do it."

Why Liverpool are ready to make Barcola third £100m signing

Barcola's family have been with him on every step of his journey, from starting out as the shy boy who played for his local team AS Buers Villeurbanne to joining Lyon's academy at the age of eight, to making his Lyon debut 11 years later, to becoming a double Champions League winner with PSG in Budapest in May.

Born Bradley Jean-Manuel Essolisam Addo Barcola on 2 September 2002, he has five siblings - including one other footballer, his older brother Malcolm, 27, a goalkeeper for Ittihad Tanger in Morocco and the Togo national team.

It was their mother who encouraged them to take up football - she would attend their matches and film the brothers playing.

"It's rare but she's the one who gave us passion [for the sport]," Barcola, who looked up to Cristiano Ronaldo and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, said in an interview with Uefa in 2024.

His father, Yves, had a passion for sport and a strong work ethic, and would gather them in the family living room to watch clips of their matches back together.

Malcolm has spoken about growing up with his younger brother.

"Every weekend, we went to the local stadium," he told newspaper Le Progres. , external "My father made Bradley do specific work in front of goal, and me, as a goalkeeper... he made me work too. We complemented each other well."

Long before Barcola, graduates from Lyon's academy included Karim Benzema, who has won multiple Champions Leagues with Real Madrid and the Ballon d'Or, Arsenal FA Cup winner Alexandre Lacazette, and France 2018 World Cup winners Samuel Umtiti and Corentin Tolisso.

More recent graduates include Manchester City forward Rayan Cherki and Chelsea full-back Malo Gusto.

Aged 17, Barcola scored 11 goals in 17 league matches for Lyon's Under-19 team before signing his first professional contract two years later in 2021.

It was a huge moment for the Barcola family.

During his rise to fame and fortune, Barcola has spoken about the importance of his family in keeping him grounded.

When the player was roundly criticised for missing chances against Newcastle in the Champions League in his first season at PSG, he turned to his family for support.

"My parents and I talk about everything," Barcola said in an interview with French newspaper Le Parisien. "As soon as something goes wrong, on or off the pitch, we talk about it. I've got my older brother, too.

"When things aren't going so well, I need to see them and get their advice.

"When they tell me 'you're messing up', it's because they're right. And when they tell me I've played well, it's because I have. I don't listen to what's said outside."

Asked about his son's reaction to the criticism following the Newcastle match, Yves Barcola said: "We talked to him about it, it's the kind of thing that doesn't affect him. That's what he tells us, it pushes him to do more.

"He's never been given anything in his young career, he's always had to earn things with his patience and qualities."

Paris St-Germain boss Luis Enrique has described Barcola as a "balanced person, very sensible, humble, hard-working, with great family values".

"After Newcastle at the Parc, he was very criticised, unfairly, and that did not reflect reality," added Luis Enrique. "He was able to calmly manage the difficult moments post- Newcastle in the best possible way."

What strengths might Barcola bring to Anfield?

'Liverpool have to get Barcola deal done'

'Iraola the right man to improve Barcola'

Barcola is the statement signing Liverpool fans have craved all summer.

With his expensive price tag, however, comes pressure.

He will be expected to hit the ground running, but he does have form against Premier League opposition.

Barcola has come up against numerous English clubs during his time at PSG. He scored in a 4-2 Champions League win over Manchester City in January 2025 before finding the net in each leg against Chelsea in the last-16 last season.

Liverpool and their new boss Andoni Iraola will take positives that Barcola settled so quickly after his high-profile move to PSG.

"He went to Paris St-Germain for something like 50m euros, which was a huge amount considering he had only played something like one full season in Ligue 1," said Minonzio.

"It was an insane amount of money for someone who had not really done anything, but Luis Enrique saw something in him.

"Luis Enrique said: 'Whatever it costs, we need him because he has huge potential.'

"Full credit to Luis Enrique because he saw things a lot of people didn't see.

"Barcola started well at PSG but after some months he had some issues because opposition defenders noticed that he was always doing the same kind of dribble.

"He was aware of that and he managed to change and have a wider range of tricks.

"He has a lot more qualities than two or three years ago."

Minonzio added: "Personally I think Liverpool is a good fit for Barcola, especially because of Iraola. He is so good at improving players and Barcola is not the finished product.

"Sometimes he runs and runs and runs, and then his finishing is not always good. He has to improve and I think he will.

"It was exactly the same with Ousmane Dembele. Two or three years ago, Dembele was so good at dribbling and running, but sometimes when he was in front of goal he was making bad choices.

"Barcola is a bit like that in the finishing aspect of his game, but he will improve with the right manager - and I think Iraola is the right manager."

Sylvain Ripoll was Barcola's France Under-21 coach in 2023.

"He's very endearing, always in a good mood," he said of Liverpool 's new signing.

"He might seem a little reserved, but he has character on the pitch and in his decision-making. He brings something different to the table, all with an exceptional mindset."

Luis Enrique has gone on record as saying signing Barcola in 2023 was a "gamble".

articles.title: Hector Fort bids emotional farewell to Barcelona: ‘I am and always will be a Culer’
articles.summary: Barcelona confirmed that they had reached an agreement for the transfer of Hector Fort to Real Sociedad this summer.The 20-year-old defender has said goodbye...
articles.body:
Barcelona confirmed that they had reached an agreement for the transfer of Hector Fort to Real Sociedad this summer.

The 20-year-old defender has said goodbye to Barcelona with an emotional message, bringing an end to a journey that began when he was just seven years old.

The young defender reflected on his deep connection with Barça, having been born only a short distance from the Spotify Camp Nou and grown up in Les Corts before spending 13 years wearing the club's colours.

"I was born just a few metres from the Camp Nou, into a family and a neighbourhood that feel the colours of this club like no other," Fort wrote in his farewell message.

He then looked back to the beginning of his journey at Barcelona.

"At seven years old, everything started for that kid from Les Corts who played in the square and ended up wearing the shirt of the club he had always felt was his."

Fort made it clear that reaching the first team was not simply a professional milestone, but the fulfilment of a family dream.

"There are no words to express what it has meant for me to have had the luck to fulfil the dream of my family and, of course, mine."

Thirteen years wearing the Barcelona badge

He recalled joining Barcelona at seven and described representing the first team as the fulfilment of both his own dream and that of his family.

"Wearing these colours, winning titles and carrying this badge on my chest for 13 years has been one of the most beautiful things that has happened to me in life, because I am and always will be a Culer ," he added.

Fort also thanked those who helped him throughout his development and the supporters who continued to back him during his time at the club.

"Thank you very much to everyone who has been part of these years, to the people who supported me without hesitation and to those who continue supporting me every day."

Fort leaves, but Barcelona stays with him

The final part of his message focused on the next step in his career.

"Now it is time to continue my path away from home, but I will always carry with me the values of Barça, everything this club has taught me and the pride of having grown up here," he revealed.

Hector Fort says goodbye to Barcelona. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images)

He closed with a simple but emotional goodbye: "See you soon, Culers . Visca el Barça !"

Fort was widely regarded as one of the biggest talents coming through La Masia , but he has broken through at a time when there is immense competition in the first team.

Although the Spaniard has always impressed with his limited first-team opportunities, at 20, he would want to be at a club where he gets regular game time.

Real Sociedad are the perfect club for Fort to continue his development. With regular minutes and a settled base, he could go on to become the player that his potential suggests.

Barcelona retain significant control over the 20-year-old's future and, as Fort puts it, this might be a "see you soon" rather than a "goodbye". It remains to be seen how the youngster gets on at the Basque club.

articles.summary: El técnico y su rival de mañana han cruzado sus caminos con polémica. El dardo a Pellegrini, la suplencia de Iker en La Rosaleda, el insulto de Jesualdo Ferreira...
articles.body: La visita del Málaga al Bernabéu trae muchos recuerdos de la primera etapa de Jose Mourinho en España. El técnico portugués tuvo al conjunto blanquiazul enfrente en algunos de los momentos más picantes de su primer periodo como entrenador madridista. La primera suplencia de Iker Casillas fue en La Rosaleda; contra Pellegrini tuvo su primer encontronazo cuando aseguró que, si el Madrid le despedía, él no iría al Málaga. Incluso en su primera visita a La Rosaleda hubo polémica por parte del lado malaguista cuando se desvelaba la historia de que Jesualdo Ferreira, técnico del Málaga por aquel entonces, había llamado burro a Mou en unas declaraciones en Portugal. Aquella fue sonada y Ferreira vetó a MARCA en Málaga durante algunas jornadas por aquello. Aunque, sin duda, de todas las mencionadas, la que más sigue retumbando es la de Iker Casillas y su suplencia contra el Málaga en la campaña 2012-2013. La cara de Florentino Pérez descubriendo en directo en las cámaras de Movistar, con Mónica Marchante, que el capitán y portero era suplente y que jugaba Adán sigue siendo uno de los clips más recurrentes en las redes sociales casi 14 años después. No le salió bien la jugada a Mourinho, que acabó perdiendo aquel partido por tres goles a dos. El entrenador portugués lo vendió como una simple decisión técnica en sala de prensa, pero la historia dejó claro con el paso del tiempo que ahí había algo más. La otra polémica situación de Mourinho ante el Málaga sigue escociendo en la capital de la Costa del Sol. En el primer año de Mourinho al frente del Real Madrid, las comparaciones con el equipo que había dirigido Pellegrini la temporada anterior fueron algo que se repitió a diario en sala de prensa. El portugués dejó entonces un recado al técnico chileno cuando trataron de poner frente a frente ambos proyectos. Y el Málaga también salió salpicado en el camino. "Bastaba con pasar la primera eliminatoria de Copa... Si el Real Madrid me echa, yo no voy a entrenar al Málaga. Me voy a un gran club de Inglaterra o de Italia”, espetó Mourinho a los medios. Pellegrini, fiel a su estilo elegante y alejado de cualquier polémica, prefirió no entrar en el juego y respondió con la misma serenidad que le caracterizaba: "No comento las opiniones de otros colegas”. Meses más tarde, y tras la anterior derrota 3-2 mencionada en párrafos anteriores, Mourinho fue de nuevo cuestionado por esto. "Nunca entrenaría al Málaga, como nunca entrenaría a muchos clubes. Soy libre de decidir dónde quiero trabajar. No tengo nada en contra del club ni de la ciudad, simplemente tengo mis preferencias para entrenar”. Historia del fútbol español e historia MARCA de este Real Madrid - Málaga del domingo.

articles.title: Mourinho wins over everyone at Real Madrid after rapid dressing room transformation
articles.summary: When Florentino Perez appointed Jose Mourinho as the new manager ahead of the 2026-27 season, there were some concerns.For all his credentials over the years...
articles.body:
When Florentino Perez appointed Jose Mourinho as the new manager ahead of the 2026-27 season, there were some concerns.

For all his credentials over the years, the Portuguese tactician's career has been on a downward trajectory for a while now.

However, according to AS , the appointment of Mourinho has worked like a charm, and the mood inside Valdebebas has changed dramatically in just two months.

The report claims that there is one phrase being repeated inside the club: "The best signing is on the bench." It is a direct reference to Mourinho.

Mourinho arrived at Real Madrid for his second stint determined to change habits, rules and customs around the first team.

His priority was to restore respect for the badge, but also to rebuild the internal standards of a squad that had become disconnected and uninspired over the previous two seasons.

Jose Mourinho has changed the mood at the Valdebebas. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

That has meant clear conversations with players about what he expects from them, while those who appeared to be heading towards the exit were given the opportunity to change their situation.

The key point is that Mourinho has not simply imposed authority. He has tried to convince the dressing room through dialogue. The approach appears to have worked quickly.

The belief inside Real Madrid is that Mourinho has already won over almost everyone around the team.

The squad are showing a greater commitment in training and a stronger willingness to compete until the final minute of matches.

This spirit was visible in Real Madrid's first two La Liga games against Espanyol and Real Sociedad, where the team seemed to be playing for one another.

Los Blancos have always had elite talent. The concern was whether that talent was operating as a unified team with clear standards.

In the last couple of seasons, Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa failed to get the group to rally around one another.

Xabi Alonso failed to get the squad to rally around him at Real Madrid. (Photo by Brendon Thorne/Getty Images)

Mourinho's first success appears to have been restoring that collective edge.

A huge leap of faith by Florentino Perez

Florentino Perez needed to send out a statement this summer after two successive trophyless seasons.

Perez and Mourinho remained in occasional contact during the 13 years between his two spells, while Jorge Mendes played an important role in facilitating the return.

The Portuguese tactician has received immense backing in terms of transfers this summer in a bid to set this project up for success.

Perez's gamble of reappointing Mourinho at a time when his stock was at its lowest is a double-edged sword.

If it works, as it seems to be doing so far, it could turn out to be a masterstroke from Perez, and it remains to be seen how the decision turns out.

articles.body:
Konstantinos Karetsas (18) said he enjoyed the crowd in a full Signal Iduna Park after Borussia Dortmund's 2-0 win against Hamburg on Saturday.

The Black and Yellows kicked off their Bundesliga season with an important three points, with the new signing playing a key role. Karetsas grabbed an assist on his league debut and put on a solid performance throughout. After the game, he stated that he enjoyed his first game in the German top flight.

"I really enjoyed my first Bundesliga game. It was my first time playing in front of the Yellow Wall with all the fans! It was so loud. That was the best part for me today. During every significant play, we could hear the whole stadium. This is a new experience for me, and I'm incredibly grateful for it," he told Sky Germany after the game.

Karetsas had four shots in the game, of which three were on target. He also completed four out of his six attempted dribbles. The winger, who joined from Genk in the summer for €30m, continued his great pre-season form into the Bundesliga and hopes the team will improve in the coming games.

"In the end, I lacked a bit of efficiency. I should have scored. We need to work on our efficiency as a team in upcoming games as well. We need to take it one game at a time now. With our fans behind us, anything is possible," he stated.

articles.title: Barcelona – Inter Milan swap deal for defenders has ‘zero possibility’ of happening – Romano
articles.summary: Alejandro Balde is one of the only first-team regulars to not feature for a single minute under Hansi Flick this season.While Joao Cancelo remains above him...
articles.body:
Alejandro Balde is one of the only first-team regulars to not feature for a single minute under Hansi Flick this season.

While Joao Cancelo remains above him on the pecking order, Xavi Espart has emerged as a surprise candidate for the left-back position and is also ahead of Balde, making his situation at the club increasingly complicated.

The player is said to have had a meeting with Hansi Flick recently where he committed his loyalty to the club and agreed to fight for his place.

Despite that, however, there was talk late last night of the player entering a possible swap deal with Inter Milan .

As the report conveyed, Barcelona and the Serie A side were said to be in talks over an exchange deal involving Balde and Federico Dimarco in what came as a shocking report.

Could Dimarco arrive this summer? (Photo by James Worsfold/Getty Images)

Fabrizio Romano , however, has maintained that there is no such discussion and has once again come out to deny any possibility of the deal happening.

The Italian journalist has now come out to say that there is zero chance and possibility of Balde and Dimarco being swapped. He insists it is just a passing rumour and that there will be no deal between Barcelona and Inter Milan.

Furthermore, he goes a step ahead to claim that not only will the deal not go through but that nothing has ever been initiated on this front. Romano stands firm that the entire story is a fabricated claim.

With Espart starting both games for Barcelona this season and completing all 180 minutes, even Joao Cancelo has found himself restricted to the bench.

Balde is expected to stay at Barcelona. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

There is no doubt that the Portuguese star will eventually return as a starter and that his fitness is currently being managed with caution, but Espart has not given the manager even the slightest reason to drop him.

In such a situation, the La Masia graduate will become Flick's preferred backup for Cancelo over Alejandro Balde, seemingly leaving the latter as a third-choice.

Having been a starter for Barcelona year after year, it will be discomforting for Balde to see his starting privileges taken away from him so suddenly, but Flick has already given him a clear blueprint of what he must do to get back his importance.

articles.standfirst: El guardameta argentino recala en el Chelsea procedente del Aston Villa por menos de nueve millones de euros
articles.summary: El guardameta argentino recala en el Chelsea procedente del Chelsea por menos de nueve millones de euros
articles.body: Durante los últimos años, ha habido varios guardametas que han cambiado la portería de Stamford Bridge por la del Emirates Stadium. Es el caso de Peter Cech y Kepa Arrizabalaga. El ‘Dibu’ Martínez, aunque con algún que otro ‘puente’ por el camino, ha emprendido el camino contrario: abandona el Aston Villa de Unai Emery y recala en el nuevo Chelsea de Xabi Alonso. La operación, tal y como adelantó David Ornstein en The Athletic, se ha cerrado por un montante que se queda ligeramente por debajo de los nueve millones de euros. Llega, además, con un contrato que le garantiza dos años y tiene la opción de extenderlo por otra temporada más. Ya el verano pasado, el ‘Dibu’ Martínez estuvo muy cerca de abandonar el Aston Villa. Llegó, incluso, a despedirse de los aficionados una vez concluida la última jornada de la Premier. El Manchester United parecía dispuesto a ficharlo. Sin embargo, se acabaron decantando por Lammens… y el guardameta argentino se quedó una temporada más en Villa Park para terminar ganando la Europa League. A pesar de tener contrato todavía hasta 2029, los rumores no se han apaciguado a lo largo de todo el verano. En esta ocasión, era la Juventus quien parecía estar en carrera ante la posible llegada de Suzuki al PSG. Todo, sin embargo, saltó por los aires: el japonés fue fichado por el propio Aston Villa y la ‘Vecchia Signora’ acordó la cesión de Vicario con el Tottenham. Fue tras el estreno de la Premier contra el Fulham, donde la actuación de Robert Sánchez dejó bastantes dudas, cuando desde el Chelsea se comenzó a acelerar la operación. Ahora, eso sí, queda por resolver qué implicaciones provoca esta decisión en la portería ‘blue’. Sobre todo, en relación a la figura de un Mike Penders que, ahora mismo, pasaría a ser el tercer portero de la plantilla. El ‘Dibu’, de este modo, abandona un Aston Villa que le propulsó a convertirse en uno de los mejores porteros del mundo: una Europa League, dos clasificaciones a Champions y 80 porterías a cero en los 256 partidos que ha disputado a lo largo de estas seis temporadas y media. Con la salida del ‘Dibu’, la columna vertebral que había fortificado Unai Emery en el Aston Villa sigue perdiendo efectivos: Konsa puso rumbo al Arsenal, Tielemans al Manchester United y Morgan Rogers, como el portero argentino, al Chelsea. No será el último, puesto que Olie Watkins está cerrando su fichaje por Al Hilal.

articles.title: Lozano's homecoming goal won't erase defensive collapse as LA Galaxy fall to San Diego
articles.summary: SAN DIEGO -- For a few minutes, it looked like Hirving Lozano’s return to Snapdragon Stadium might turn into the kind of night the LA Galaxy had been waiting...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO -- For a few minutes, it looked like Hirving Lozano's return to Snapdragon Stadium might turn into the kind of night the LA Galaxy had been waiting for.

Lozano had spent nearly 10 months away from competitive action, and San Diego made sure he knew exactly how it felt to come back.

He was booed the first time he touched the ball and was fouled repeatedly as the match grew more physical. Then, after San Diego went down a man early in the second half, Lozano finally found his moment.

A loose ball bounced around the penalty area before falling to Lozano, who made no mistake from close range. He celebrated in front of the Galaxy supporters who had made the trip, embracing the moment in a stadium where his return carried plenty of weight.

For the Galaxy, though, the goal was part of a much larger night that slipped away in a 3-1 loss to San Diego FC on Saturday.

"It was great for him to score because I think confidence builds off of situations like that," head coach Greg Vanney said.

Lozano looked the part of a player still finding his rhythm, but one who could immediately give the Galaxy another attacking option. His directness helped create opportunities, including the sequence that eventually led to San Diego's red card and his own goal.

"I worked very hard all this time to get to this, to play 90 minutes," Lozano said. "I'm going step by step, improving. I had a lot of time without playing, and every game those doubts are going away."

Vanney also liked what he saw from Lozano emotionally, particularly given the circumstances of his return.

"I thought he handled himself like a professional," Vanney said. "He played with emotion, but not with too much emotion."

That progress may be one of the few encouraging developments the Galaxy can take from a night that exposed another problem they have spent much of 2026 trying to solve.

San Diego repeatedly found space behind and between the Galaxy's defensive lines. The first goal came in the 11th minute when Anders Dreyer kept the ball alive and found Elias Achouri in the box. Kieran Sargant then slipped past Harbor Miller just two minutes into the second half to make it 2-0.

The Galaxy spent too much of the first half caught between pressing high and sitting deeper, allowing San Diego's attackers to find pockets in the middle of the field.

"We were kind of in between those two things a little bit too often, and they were able to pick us apart at times," Vanney said.

The problem resurfaced even after the Galaxy were given a lifeline.

Jeppe Tverskov's second yellow card left San Diego with 10 men, and Lozano's goal pulled the Galaxy within one. They briefly thought they had completed the comeback when Kyogo Furuhashi finished another Lozano-created chance, but VAR ruled that Lozano had committed a foul in the buildup.

Vanney strongly disagreed with the decision, arguing that the officiating lacked a consistent standard throughout the match.

"The whole game had varying levels of what's a foul and what's not a foul," he said.

He pointed to several other decisions involving Joseph Paintsil and argued that the standard seemed to shift throughout the night. Still, Vanney did not let the officiating completely off the hook for what happened.

The Galaxy were a man up and had momentum. Instead of finding an equalizer, they conceded again when Amahl Pellegrino finished a San Diego transition.

"I think we lose an opportunity because you've got to be able to manage situations like that that occur in the game," Vanney said.

The Galaxy had finally wrestled control of the match away from San Diego. Once the equalizer disappeared, though, the game became frantic, and they never found their footing again.

Lozano's return showed the Galaxy may finally have another attacking piece capable of changing a game. Sergio Roberto's debut also gave Vanney a glimpse of what the midfield could look like as the new additions settle in.

But the defense remains the larger concern.

With just one win in their last eight matches and the playoff race beginning to tighten, there is little room for the Galaxy to keep giving opponents openings like the ones San Diego found Saturday.

Lozano may have provided a glimpse of what could change for this team.

The Galaxy will hope that translates to points soon, starting with a return to Dignity Health Sports Park with a full week of rest on Sept. 5. Kickoff is set for 6:30 p.m.

articles.title: Arsenal offload Fabio Vieira to Hamburg as Arteta accelerates clear-out including Martinelli and Jesus exits
articles.summary: Arsenal have agreed a deal to sell Fabio Vieira to Hamburg for a fee of around £7.7m.Vieira spent last season on loan with the Bundesliga side an impressed,...
articles.body:
Arsenal have agreed a deal to sell Fabio Vieira to Hamburg for a fee of around £7.7m.

Vieira spent last season on loan with the Bundesliga side an impressed, scoring seven league goals and providing five assists in 29 appearances.

The Portugal midfielder's contribution helped Hamburg secure a 13th-place finish in the club's first campaign back in the Bundesliga after promotion.

Hamburg have now reached an agreement to sign the 26-year-old on a permanent basis for a fee of £7.7m, as Arsenal continue to reduce their squad numbers. Sky Sports are reporting that a full agreement is in place for Vieira to return to Germany.

Vieira has spent the past two seasons out on loan after failing to make an impact at Arsenal, following a £34m move to North London in 2022. He started only five Premier League games for the Gunners across two seasons, before loan spells at former club FC Porto and Hamburg.

Vieira's exit continues an active period for Arsenal in terms of sales, as Mikel Arteta looks to trim his squad. Gabriel Martinelli is set to undergo a medical at Al-Hilal after a £55m deal was agreed with the Saudi Pro League side.

The Brazilian's departure will represent a record sale for Arsenal. Elsewhere, Gabriel Jesus is set to sign for Spanish champions Barcelona. A £8.5m fee has been agreed between the teams for Jesus, whose Arsenal contract was due to expire in 2027.
